13:57.race_name: Soil Association 80th Anniversary Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Picked up well en route to being nicely on top at the finish in Windsor event; promising
runners.name: Love Is

quotes.race: Betwright Windsor Flat Season Opener Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Love Is had never been away, and you could tell at halfway because she was very raw and green, but the penny dropped and she flew home. She's a huge stride on her and she's a nice filly. We've always liked her, and she just does enough at home, but the way she quickened was lovely. I was looking at the sectionals, and she was a second quicker than any other horse in the last furlong. She's pretty smart. I'd say she'll probably end up there [Royal Ascot]. She might need another run before that, as she was so green, but we'll see. The filly, Lazurite, who was second the other day, is probably a little bit quicker than this one, but I've got a good bunch of fillies - Richard Hughes, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 90,000euros yearling; Sioux Nation half-sister to four winners; picked up well from the back and was nicely on top at the finish in Windsor event (6f, good to firm); promising filly.

runners.comment: Got on top towards the finish in Ascot contest and looks a plausible Royal Ascot hope
runners.name: Night In Vegas
runners.spotlight: 60,000gns yearling; Lucky Vega half-brother to five winners; got on top towards the finish in Ascot contest (6f, good) and looks a plausible Royal Ascot hope; respected.

runners.comment: AW winner who seems to face a stiffer task back on turf but may progress again
runners.name: Shadow King
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.spotlight: Dark Angel colt; made all at Kempton (6f, AW) to step up on his Newmarket effort (5f); appears to face a stiffer task back on turf but may be capable of further progress.

14:32.race_name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.comment: Promising second, from the front, at Newmarket on 1,000 Guineas day; leading contender
runners.name: Lazurite
runners.spotlight: Trainer rode this filly's dam to Listed 2yo success during his riding days; promising half-length second of eight, from the front, in Newmarket event (5f, good to firm) on 1,000 Guineas day; leading contender.

runners.comment: £105,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; by Persian Force and descends from a 6f 2yo Group 2 winner
runners.name: Blushrose
runners.spotlight: 82,000euros yearling, £105,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; Persian Force half-sister to 6f AW winner Jorge Alvares (RPR 97); dam unraced, is granddaughter of 6f 2yo Group 2 scorer; major stable; good credentials.

runners.comment: Penalty for narrow win at Newmarket is partly offset by Mason Paetel's useful claim
runners.name: Magic Effort

quotes.race: Scorthy Champ Standing At Barton British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Magic Effort in work the other day and she went well. Hopefully she could be a Royal Ascot filly after that - Benoit de la Sayette, jockey.

runners.spotlight: The offspring of two winners for her owner; prevailed only narrowly at the Newmarket Craven meeting (5f, good) but is open to progress and a penalty is partly offset by Mason Paetel's useful 5lb claim.

runners.comment: £105,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; by Blue Point out of 5f 2yo scorer; likely type
runners.name: Targa
runners.spotlight: £62,000 yearling, £105,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; Blue Point half-sister to three winners, notably Showtime Mahomes (5f-7f including 2yo/AW; RPR 85); dam 5f AW 2yo scorer (72); likely type.

runners.comment: Beaten favourite in two AW events, nevertheless showing ability; may still do better
runners.name: Pershaada
runners.spotlight: Beaten favourite in a couple of 5f AW contests, nevertheless showing ability, last time second behind the subsequent Marygate (Listed) winner; may still do better and it remains too early to write her off.

runners.comment: Attractively bred, by Blue Point out of a 6f 2yo winner (on debut) for her owner
runners.name: Fast Track
runners.spotlight: Attractively bred newcomer, by Blue Point out of a 6f 2yo winner (on debut; later Group placed; RPR 97) for her owner; interesting, especially if the market speaks positively.

runners.comment: Showed some promise with third of six, best of the newcomers, in Salisbury conditions race
runners.name: Babzini
runners.spotlight: Showed some promise with third of six, best of the newcomers, in Salisbury conditions race (5f, good to firm) won by quite a useful sort (Listed placed since); not difficult to envisage her going well.

runners.breeder: R F And S D Knipe
runners.comment: 42,000euros yearling; Caturra half-sister to three winners; market informative
runners.name: Lola
runners.spotlight: 17,000gns foal, 42,000euros yearling; Caturra half-sister to three winners, notably King Cuan (Group-placed 6f/7f 2yo; RPR 112); dam 7f AW/7.5f turf scorer (85); market informative.

runners.comment: 18,000euros yearling; Lucky Vega half-sister to two winners; check the betting
runners.name: Kentucky Rain
runners.spotlight: 18,000euros yearling; Lucky Vega half-sister to two winners, notably Son Of Corballis (5f 2yo including Listed; RPR 93); dam related to two UAE Oaks winners; check the betting.

runners.comment: Can set pace; unraced beyond 1m4f on Flat but can't be comfortably dismissed in this field
runners.name: Give It To Me Oj

quotes.race: Masterson Holdings Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's a cliche but Give It To Me OJ could be anything - he honestly could be. His four-year-old season was always going to be harder but we could look at the Gerry Feilden Hurdle for him - Josh Moore, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Geoff Lewis Apprentices' Derby Handicap (Supported By Betfred) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Give It To Me Oj does everything so easily, he's a very talented horse. He's one to look out for this jumps season - Ashley Lewis, jockey.

quotes.race: Sash & Dash By Quickslide Jump Jockeys Derby Handicap (For Professional Jump Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: We know Give It To Me Oj is very quick out of the stalls, so I just tried to dictate it from the front, and he's done it well. I got on well with him last season as a juvenile hurdler, but hopefully there are a few more Flat races he can win before he goes back hurdling. He's an exciting horse and we haven't seen the best of him yet - Caoilin Quinn, rider.

quotes.race: bet365 Novices' Championship Final Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Give It To Me Oj has always been a nice horse and has exceeded all our expectations today. For a four-year-old to carry 12 stone, is a very good performance. He will stick to hurdles next year. He will have a break now but he could also run on the Flat. He is still well handicapped on the Flat but we'll see how he comes out of this race. We will see what his handicap mark is, but he could start back in the Masterson Holdings Hurdle at Cheltenham or the Free Handicap Hurdle at Chepstow - Gary Moore, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Juvenile Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Apart from the last, Give It To Me OJ jumped well. He was going a bit left-handed, but that might have been because the front horse was going left-handed. Through no fault of his own he's had a messed up season, but he needed that run the other day when he was second - Gary Moore, joint-trainer.

runners.spotlight: Acts on soft; can make the running; won six (four over hurdles, two on Flat) of seven starts in a golden spell last February-October; soundly beaten over hurdles on latest three outings (in tough races on last two) and unraced beyond 1m4f on Flat, but he can't be comfortably dismissed in this small field.

stable_tour.quote: He really got things together over hurdles last winter and finished the season well when winning under top weight at Sandown on finals day. As expected, he was well handicapped back on the Flat, winning twice at Epsom over the summer and he might yet go for the November Handicap. He's a big horse who was always going to do better with time, and his quality got him through when winning from the front at Cheltenham on Saturday. He'll be better than that over hurdles, and there's a Grade 3 for four-year-olds at Fairyhouse at the end of November to consider, although the Gerry Feilden at Newbury is more likely. Beyond that, what was the Betfair Hurdle in February is the sort of stiff test he wants and the County Hurdle might suit him at the end of the season. He's a proper horse to run over hurdles. 28-10-25

runners.comment: Raced freely but close, never-nearer 3rd over C&D (good) on return was more improved form
runners.name: St Mawes

quotes.race: Close Brothers Colwick Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: We are thrilled to bits with that. We enjoyed winning last time out at Kempton Park, but we didn't quite know what would happen this time back on turf, however. I thought it was a good performance and St Mawes battled well. We thought there was talent with him, but it has been unlocking that ability and it now seems to have clicked at last. The feedback after his last win was that he had come on again. The original thought after Kempton Park was to see if he could do it again and then have a break and give him some time off over the winter before bringing him back next year, but we will chat to Emma and see what we will do - Julian Reed, owner.

runners.spotlight: Usually held up; third in a 2yo maiden was his sole run on softer than good; can race freely but showed improved form when upped to 2m for wins at Kempton (AW) and Nottingham (good) in his final two runs last season, and he continued on his upward curve when a close, never-nearer third of seven over C&D (good) three weeks ago; retains potential.

runners.comment: Fifth of 12 at Newmarket (1m6f) last time was respectable but settling him was an issue
runners.name: Bahadur
runners.owner: J William Rowley & S P C Woods
runners.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good when on turf; made immediate progress when switched to AW in the autumn, completing a hat-trick in a 1m4f novice and 1m4f/1m6f handicaps; perhaps in need of the race (albeit joint-favourite) on reappearance last month and fifth of 12 at Newmarket (1m6f) four weeks later was respectable, but settling him was an issue; suitability for a slog over 2m can therefore be questioned.

runners.breeder: C&s B/S Ltd C Younghusband K McGivern
runners.comment: AW has dominated career; best turf ratings on last two outings but still needs better
runners.name: Sax Appeal
runners.spotlight: Very busy and he's had his share of wins, including four over 2m in 2025, but that's been mostly on AW which has dominated his career; best turf ratings were on last two outings but his turf form still needs improvement.

runners.comment: 1st and 2nd in his last two Kempton AW starts; good chance if that form is transferred
runners.name: Caprelo
runners.spotlight: Close third on soft at Yarmouth (1m6f) last July was his best turf form; needs better given the improvement he's shown on Kempton AW (2m) in two of his three starts since, but he'd have a good chance if that form is transferred back to turf; won on 2024 reappearance; needs a close look.

stable_tour.quote: He's got the ability and last season he won first time out at Kempton and was second twice, but he's become disappointing. He was favourite last time at Kempton, where he finished fifth, and I'm afraid Ulysses's progeny can be a bit reluctant to put their best feet forward. He runs at Kempton again on Wednesday. 29-05-25

15:42.race_name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Made all at Ascot on handicap/seasonal debut and looks the type to progress further
runners.name: Venetia
runners.spotlight: Made all at Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) on handicap/seasonal debut, building on her 2yo efforts, and looks the type to progress further; bred to be suited by this longer distance; upped in class but receives plenty of weight all round; shortlisted.

runners.comment: Well treated under a penalty (future mark 1lb higher) and may improve further to boot
runners.name: Sibling Rivelry

quotes.race: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Sibling Rivelry got in a nice rhythm and travelled round lovely. We hit the front and I thought I was going to do it hands and heels but she idled a little bit. She's a b big filly and a nice galloping track like today's really suits here - Jack Dace, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Unraced on soft/heavy; appeared to have something in hand at Windsor (11.5f) last week on seasonal debut, taking turf record to 2-3 and overall strike-rate to 4-7; back up two grades but looks well treated under a penalty (future mark 1lb higher) and won over C&D last August; may improve further to boot; respected.

runners.comment: Steadily progressive last term, building up a solid record that featured three wins
runners.name: Orionis
runners.spotlight: Yet to race on soft/heavy ground; steadily progressive last term, building up a solid record that featured three wins; good third at Newmarket final outing; cheekpieces worn the last twice are now removed; likely to go well.

runners.comment: Held her form well last year for Richard Hughes; sold for 70,000gns since last run
runners.name: Quebella
runners.spotlight: Trained last year by Richard Hughes, winning on debut then holding her form well, including two creditable efforts at Goodwood; sold for 70,000gns since last run; the betting may help to ascertain expectations on stable/seasonal debut.

runners.comment: Has form figures of 112 when racing below Listed/Group level
runners.name: Amora Queen

quotes.race: bet365 EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We all came here hoping to see Amora Queen win a bit more impressively, but the fact we thought she might still be raw was why we're here and not in better company. We actually thought about taking this filly to the Star Stakes at Sandown, but Jaber actually won that with another filly [Hope Queen], who beat my runner [Jennifer Jane] on the line, very frustratingly - Charlie Johnston, trainer.Amora Queen has done what's needed. She's a big girl, but she's got a good engine - Jaber Abdullah, owner.

quotes.race: Yorkshire Air Ambulance EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Has Waldgeist ever had a June two-year-old winner? Have a look at the size and shape of Amora Queen, what's she going to be next year? - Mark Johnston, trainer's father.

runners.spotlight: Well beaten in the Lingfield Oaks Trial most recently but is somewhat interesting back down in grade, being a filly who has form figures of 112 when racing below Listed/Group level; ran well in Doncaster handicap (1m2f) the final time.

stable_tour.quote: She's a huge, scopey filly and was probably achieving ahead of her time last year. We bit off more than we could chew in the Fillies' Mile and an Oaks entry is probably ambitious at this stage, but she should stay very well and it wouldn't be a huge surprise if she improved enough over middle distances to be up to having a shot at something like that. The tentative route would be to reappear in a fillies' handicap at Doncaster on Saturday, or the slightly more ambitious route would be the Cheshire Oaks. She showed a good level of ability at two and has always looked like she'll be much better at three, which is quite exciting. She's wintered very well and had a racecourse gallop at the Craven meeting. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Absent since creditable second in last year's November Handicap on stable debut
runners.name: Miss Dolly Rocker
runners.spotlight: Five-time winner, including over C&D; absent since creditable second in last year's November Handicap at Doncaster on debut for new yard; hit with another rise in the weights but drops back in class and may remain competitive.

runners.comment: Three-time AW scorer; below par returned to turf last time; this is harder
runners.name: Charmaine
runners.spotlight: Three-time AW scorer; turf form features two good efforts but she's 0-4 in this sphere and was below par at Doncaster most recently; not the percentage call in this warmer contest.

runners.comment: Consistent AW handicapper; faces difficult task off current mark back on turf
runners.name: Caramay
runners.spotlight: Consistent AW handicapper and a seven-time winner in that sphere; only 1-9 on turf and appears to have a difficult task off current mark, especially in this grade, returned to this sphere.

runners.comment: Has a doubt over current form and is the oldest and most exposed contender
runners.name: Typical Woman
runners.spotlight: Ended her 2025 campaign with an August win but hasn't been in anything like the same form since returning to action and is the most exposed, as well as the oldest, contender in this field.

runners.comment: Lightly raced; may do better still; a possible danger, provided she stays new trip
runners.name: Time Loop
runners.spotlight: Stablemate of Orionis; lightly raced 5yo who wasn't disgraced on handicap debut (1m2f; kept to AW) when last seen; showed promise on debut in sole turf attempt and may do better still; possible danger, provided she stays the new trip.

runners.comment: Creditable third in Chester Group 2 upped to 1m2f last time; unexposed at this trip
runners.name: Ice Max
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

quotes.race: PricedUp Robin Hood Stakes (Listed Race) (Formerly Known As The Ben Marshall Stakes)
quotes.quote: After the first couple of furlongs Ice Max got into a nice rhythm. He's grown up a lot, he's strong and he's definitely a Group horse - Shane Gray, rider speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: William Hill Autumn Mile Handicap
quotes.quote: Ice Max has been running consistently in Group 2s and Group 3s. He likes cut in the ground and a flat out gallop - James Cowley, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Diomed Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Ice Max is a bit of a hard one to place as he needs soft ground, and I just think he was in front half a furlong too soon there. If the leader had led us a bit further he would have just sat, but he committed and took a length out of the winner and then just got outstayed. A shame, but he ran well - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Celebration Mile Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Before the race we knew Ice Max would love the soft ground. We didn't go very quick but he travelled very well. Once I switched over to the stands' side rail, I knew I'd won it from there - Clifford Lee, rider.

runners.spotlight: Won the Celebration Mile at Goodwood in 2024; creditable third, faring best of the runners who came off steady pace, in Group 2 at Chester (good) upped to 1m2f last time; unexposed at this distance and enters calculations despite carrying a 3lb penalty for Listed success (1m, soft) last autumn.

stable_tour.quote: A solid horse who finished off last season really well. A free-going type who doesn't always settle, he saw out his last two races well and will hopefully carry on in that vein. He wants soft ground and we'll probably start him off over a mile. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Smart performer whose strong CV features two Royal Ascot wins; major contender
runners.name: Haatem

quotes.race: Wolferton Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I think James [Doyle] did [when asked who made the decision to aim at the Wolferton]. As much as it pains me to say, he said in France 'Haatem doesn't feel like he has the speed for a mile so let's step up'. He chose this race and, to me, he never looked like getting beaten today. He's just such a lovely horse, a gentleman, whenever he runs there's a lot of love for him in the office, emails and things. He's pleased everybody all the way along the line, especially me. He's in it [the Eclipse] and he'll run very well. Rosallion will go to the Sussex and this horse probably will go to the Eclipse - Richard Hannon, trainer.I was quietly confident, because of how well Haatem relaxes. Then we jumped out the gates from a lowish draw ? I wanted to make sure he jumped good, then I couldn't get him back for the first two, he was fighting me! So then I wasn't completely convinced, but once we got into Swinley Bottom he took a breath and relaxed all the way up to the hill. I had a nice draught into the race, where I didn't have to go looking for gaps. I was a little bit patient. I was lucky, the gaps kind of opened and I didn't really have to come round the horse and he picked up really good. He's tough. Once I got upsides Galen, I knew he would keep fighting, because that's one of the best qualities he has, is he is tough in a fight - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Jersey Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Haatem is a pleasure to have around and I would love to think we will have an association for a few years to come. He deserved his day in the sun and hopefully there will be many more. He was very unlucky in the Woodcote and it was probably my fault because I kept running him over six furlongs. Both Jamie Spencer and James Doyle both said he won't have a problem going to seven furlongs and they were right, again! He carried a 3lb penalty today, he got to the front very easy and I'm just delighted for the horse. It's a Group 3 but I think this Jersey was an awful lot more than it normally is. He has credit for a lot more than that I'm sure a Group 1 is coming very soon - Richard Hannon, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Craven Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Haatem is a good horse and always has been. He won a Vintage Stakes with a subsequent Champagne Stakes winner behind him and was fifth in a Dewhurst last year. I said to Sean that I thought he'd get the trip very well and it seems to be this week that horses that race handy are winning. I don't think you can say that was an average performance. He looked pretty good there. He has done it on the racecourse and 25-1 seems to be a little bit generous for the Guineas. He and Rosallion do a lot of work together, Rosallion is a horse with an awful lot of speed whereas this horse gets a trip extremely well. Rosallion will get the mile and they both will probably run. We've made no secret about how special we think Rosallion is and this horse surprised me with the manner of his win today. It is nice to have two very good milers on our hands with two very good chances. I think one has an exceptional chance and one now has a better chance than he had before - Richard Hannon, trainer.

quotes.race: Nicholson Gin Vintage Stakes (Group 2) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Haatem is a lovely horse and he deserved that after running so well in the Coventry and the Superlative. He was very unlucky in the Woodcote. I thought this was his day and could be his Derby, but he will get better as the year goes on and he is a horse big enough for next year. He's not about being a two-year-old, he ran here first time and he has improved all year. He is a Group 2 winner now, so obviously we will have to look at Group 1s, but he is getting better - Richard Hannon, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Superlative Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with that, we've always thought a lot of Haatem and he's got a bright future. Next year will probably be his year, he's in a few nice races towards the end of the year, he'll probably be better on a sound surface. He takes his racing very well and physically he's a very nice horse. The winner looks a very good one - Richard Hannon, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Has form on all types of ground; smart performer whose strong CV includes wins in the Vintage Stakes at Goodwood as a 2yo and two Royal Ascot contests, more recently last year's Wolferton (1m2f Listed); best figures give him a major chance at the weights.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a real star for us, winning at Royal Ascot for the last two seasons, so we'll try to get a race into him before heading there again, although I may just do it with a couple of racecourse gallops. The Wolferton will be his target again. He showed he got the trip when winning it last year, so we'll work back from that. He's sound, honest, versatile and very good. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Respected on ratings and is a similar type to last year's winner (for same connections)
runners.name: Boiling Point
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

quotes.race: bet365 Cambridgeshire (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Boiling Point is a very good horse and is really a Group horse - he will win a good Group race. But Cliff [Lee, jockey] is so good from the front. There was no point pulling him round, even with top-weight. It was all about getting him into a nice rhythm and he was either going to be good enough or he wasn't. We were always going to go far side from that draw (6) and it has worked out really well. I don't know how much weight exactly he was giving the second, but he's just held on. He was running on fumes for the last 100 yards but as I say Cliff is brilliant from the front and I'm never worried when I ask him to go forward. He will go back into Group company now. I don't know where yet - today was the plan - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill King Charles II Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Boiling Point nearly won a Group Three here at the end of last year. He has got away with it today, but he will be better on good to firm ground. He has looked like he needed every yard of it today. I need to speak his owner Sheikh Obaid but he has had two quick runs now and I would quite like to put him away and wait for the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot. The stiff seven furlongs there should suit him and I thought all through the winter that it could be the race for him. After that, we can decide whether we step him up to a mile. In my opinion, it looks like he would stay a mile - Roger Varian, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Defied top weight in the 2025 Cambridgeshire (1m1f, good to firm) and holds a leading chance provided that smart handicap form is reproduced; hasn't transferred it back to Group level this term but he's respected on ratings and is a similar type to last year's winner of this race (for same connections).

stable_tour.quote: Won the Cambridgeshire last year with a really solid performance. We stepped him up in trip in the Winter Derby and while I think he gets a mile and a quarter, the track didn't suit. He could go for the Earl of Sefton at Newmarket next. 31-03-26

He has always looked a nice colt and I expected him to go well on his debut, which he did when finishing second to Cogitate at Newbury over 7f. That did him a lot of good and we sent him back there over a mile on Friday, when he finished third. We'll have to sit down and see where he goes next. 25-08-23

runners.comment: Ties in with Haatem on 2025 Royal Ascot running; returns from ten-month layoff
runners.name: Enfjaar
runners.owner: T & Mrs L Standish & Mrs A Spence

quotes.race: John Smith's Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Enfjaar had bone bruising among some other things last year, but Jack rode him in work last week and he looked good. This was a tough race, though, but we won it two years ago with a horse who went and won a Group 1. I'm not saying this fella will, but I hope he will! We'll reassess and see where they put him, but he'll probably be out of handicaps and into Group races now. There's lots of lovely races in Britain and abroad. He's exciting - Richard Hills, owners' representative.

runners.spotlight: Unlucky second at Glorious Goodwood in 2024 when bidding for a notable 1m2f handicap double; best effort in a truncated 2025 campaign when fourth to Haatem in Listed grade at Royal Ascot; should be thereabouts, provided he's in top form after ten-month layoff.

stable_tour.quote: We trained him for the Wolferton last season and he was unlucky not to win. He looks as good as ever and he's likely to start back in the Listed Festival Stakes at Goodwood in May. How he goes there will dictate his early-season programme. If he wasn't to win, he could go back to the Wolferton, but if he won at Goodwood we might be more ambitious. He hasn't been over-raced and is a lovely older horse to have around. 01-04-26

runners.comment: His most promising runs are not forgotten and it's too soon to give up on him; new trip
runners.name: La Botte
runners.owner: Halo Racing N Greenhalgh J Degenhardt
runners.spotlight: Unlucky second in last year's Britannia at Royal Ascot then caught the eye on reappearance; hasn't exactly lived up to expectations in two starts since but remains of interest assuming this new scenario (steps up from 1m) prompts a positive effect; too soon to give up on him.

runners.comment: Had the run of the race when 33-1 winner of similar event over C&D last September
runners.name: Naqeeb

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Foundation Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We're absolutely thrilled with the result and delighted for Naqeeb as well. He's run some big races in defeat this year, so it's lovely to see him get his head in front. His starting price probably reflected his chance, but he's a decent animal and it was a case of having a go and trying something different. I'm thrilled for Ryan [Sexton], who rode him very well, he had him in the perfect position and committed him at the right time - Steve Brown, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes (Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Very pleased with Naqeeb. He's woken up a lot from Haydock. I thought initially when I rode him that he takes a while to get going; today he probably travelled too well early and was taking me into nice positions. He's unlucky on the day, but he's a horse we're learning about and I think we'll have loads of fun with him - Ryan Sexton, jockey

quotes.race: Get Daily Rewards With Betfair Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought 100 was steep for Naqeeb but I think he's improved a bit for going up in trip and he'll be a good stayer next year. He's not as quick as Baaeed - he wants another mile - but he's a big raw horse who still has lots to learn and I suspect one more [run this season] if we're lucky. He's useful and if he can end up half as good as those two [Baaeed and Hukum] that'll do me. He took a long time to win and then got mugged by Middle Earth at Newmarket, and now look at Middle Earth who has a likely chance in the Leger - William Haggas, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Performed well twice over C&D last term but had the run of the race when belying his 33-1 odds for neck success at Listed level in September (good to soft) and looks no certainty to defy a 3lb penalty back here, unless things again fall his way.

stable_tour.quote: We really like him. He was third at Royal Ascot in the Duke of Edinburgh and we were thrilled with him as it showed he has a good race in him, but he just got too far back in the John Smith's Cup at York last time and you've got to put a line through that and move on from it. We'll try to see if we can get him to the 1m2f handicap at Goodwood next Tuesday. We're not discouraged from trying him again over that trip. He's more or less run every two or three weeks of late, so it just depends on what he's telling us. He's a nice horse to have. 23-07-25

runners.comment: Retains plenty of ability but has something to find back on home soil
runners.name: Involvement

quotes.race: Downtown Dash (Handicap) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I didn't ride Involvement last time but I had a kind draw here, the pace picked up some way out and everything was smooth - Silvestre De Sousa, jockey, speaking to Racing Dubai.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Involvement has won it really well and stepping him up to a mile and a quarter made the difference. The Britannia didn't really play to his abilities but we've always held this horse in very high regard and I think he can keep improving - Simon Crisford, joint trainer.

quotes.race: British EBF Supports Racing To School Future Stayers Maiden Stakes (Sire & Dam Restricted) (GBB)
quotes.quote: That was a pleasing start and Involvement picked up really nicely. He's got no targets at this stage and we'll see how he is over the next few weeks and make a plan from there - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer.

runners.spotlight: Missed 2025; last two performances, namely success at Meydan (handicap) and third at Longchamp (Listed), show that he retains plenty of ability; however, has something to find back on home soil.

runners.comment: Age may be catching up with him; hasn't won a domestic race since 2023
runners.name: Certain Lad

quotes.race: La Coupe de Maisons-Laffitte (Group 3) (4yo+) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Certain Lad was always a good horse, he won the Strensall as a four-year-old but had a couple of nasty injuries at five and six. This is the first year he's come into a season with no injury. He's sound and well, and a happy horse. He's got a great mind and is easy to train because he wants to do it. The two races for him are the Preis von Europa over a mile and a half or the Prix Dollar. I think I'll probably lean towards the Prix Dollar, but I'd love to run him in a Group 1 at some stage. He'll stay in training at nine and we'll see if he retains the same zest. We might have a look at something like the Prix Ganay at the start of the year. He's an eight-year-old and I won't have too much longer with him, so we won't mess around, we'll run him in some nice races - Jack Channon, trainer.

quotes.race: Red Rock Partnership Recruitment Solutions Handicap
quotes.quote: Certain Lad was rated 112, he's come back down to 100 (before York) and he's back to a mark he can win off, it's as simple as that really. He's still a very good horse, even at seven. He was a Listed winner as a two-year-old, he was third in the Railway Stakes and has won in Dubai. The handicapping system is there for a reason, he's come down and won two very nice races now. It has been discussed in the office a few times, whether we missed this and went straight to the November Handicap. Let's see how he comes out of this as he's had a couple of quick runs there. If he's bouncing, which I'm sure he will be knowing him, we might have a little look at it, if not we'll keep a mile and a half up our sleeve for next year because he loves racing and he's as good an advocate as you could have for racing, so he'll be carrying on next year as well - Jack Channon, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet And Symphony Group Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Certain Lad gave me a great ride. He was stepping down in trip and he settled really well. He hit a bit of a flat spot three and a half down but we came across to the stands' side and he was very tough, once I got daylight he really ran to the line for me. The further I went the better and he thrived on the ground - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Zabeel Turf Sponsored By Riviera 1 (Listed Handicap) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Certain Lad is improving with every run. He does everything a horse should do to get himself beat, but he keeps winning. In the prelims he gets very warm and is notorious for it. He gets hot and sweaty, but it doesn't seem to bother him in the race. He ran a bit fresh and keen the first two furlongs, but once he got into a rhythm, I was delighted. He picked them up well and kept going all the way to the line - Ben Curtis, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Multiple winner down the years but 2025 figures suggest age may be catching up with him to some degree; hasn't won a domestic race since 2023 and it's an even longer time since he made a successful seasonal debut.

stable_tour.quote: He had a great season last year, winning a Listed race and a Group 3 in France. He had a very small setback after his Group win, which prevented us from having a crack at some of the big ones, but he'll be campaigned at the top level. There's no point running him with penalties in Group 3s this year. We're going to take a punt to see if we can land a big one. He'll go for the Prix d'Harcourt at Longchamp on Sunday, all being well, with a view to then going for the Prix Ganay. He'll have entries in the Prince of Wales's and all those other races, and if one cuts up he's that high-level horse who could pick up the pieces. He seems to be training well and he's our flagbearer, and we hope he can win some more stakes races this year. 02-04-25

runners.comment: Record of 0-5 since debut win but he's useful and ran creditably in sole C&D attempt
runners.name: High Stock

quotes.race: Boodles Raindance Dee Stakes (Listed Race) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: High Stock ran a great race. There are a lot of options, it depends how he comes out of this race. That was only his second run, it was a big race. Is it ten furlongs or 12? Also, how much did he learn from that race? For a second race it was quite exciting. Oisin said he cantered into the race, it almost happened too easily for him. Oisin said he could go in the King Edward VII at Royal Ascot. He's not in the Derby. He had to improve 14lb from his last run, he nearly did it! We're delighted - Anna Lisa Balding, wife of trainer Andrew Balding.

quotes.race: bet365 Wood Ditton Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: High Stock is a horse we like a lot. I thought it might be a bit sharp for him today because he is going to stay further in time. David gave him a lovely ride and he has got it done. We'll see about the future. He is not in the Dante or anything fancy. There is always Ascot if we need more time, which I think is more likely. We like him and he should improve - Andrew Balding, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Record of 0-5 since debut win (Wood Ditton) but he's useful and ran creditably in sole C&D attempt, namely fourth to Naqeeb in Listed event; could go well with Chester (Group 2) reappearance under his belt.

runners.comment: Took well to cheekpieces last time and may have more to offer in the retained headgear
runners.name: Philanthropist
runners.spotlight: Took well to first-time cheekpieces at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) returned to turf with AW reappearance under his belt, taking overall record to 3-13; upped in grade but may have more to offer in the retained headgear; shortlisted.

runners.comment: May resume progress with AW reappearance under his belt; should take well to Goodwood
runners.name: Kisskodi
runners.spotlight: Unraced on soft/heavy; scored four times on turf last term and may resume his progress with creditable AW reappearance under his belt; combined record of 3-4 at Epsom and Brighton bodes well for this first visit to Goodwood, which is quite similar to those tracks; highly respected.

runners.comment: Chance partly depends on how well he responds to removal of usual cheekpieces
runners.name: Oliver Show

quotes.race: William Hill Lincoln (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Oliver Show has run a massive race. Huge credit to Charles Eddery and Chas Robinson who brought him back from Bahrain. He's a progressive horse - I thought he was maxed out where he is but he looks like there may be a little bit left. He goes well fresh and I'd say we'll probably work back from the Royal Hunt Cup - George Boughey, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Useful on his day but losing run is mounting up and two duck eggs this year leave a question mark over his current form; chance partly depends on how well he responds to the removal of usual cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: He was meant to come back for the Lincoln but got stuck in Bahrain, where he was completely outpaced over six furlongs in January. He could go to the Guineas meeting if he gets back in time, then maybe go for this month's Spring Cup at Newbury. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Low-mileage 5yo who looks interesting back up in trip; further progress is still possible
runners.name: Walsons Law
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Lady Cobham

prev_owners.owner: Roldvale Ltd W Salthouse & E Babington

runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who has gained both wins (7f/1m) on good to firm; grabbed third place on line over 6f for an encouraging reappearance effort and looks interesting back up in distance, with further improvement still a possibility.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Windsor this month but I backed him up a bit quick - the handicapper notched him up 9lb, so I thought I had to run under a penalty. That last run was at Kempton but I don't think he's as good on the all-weather as he is on turf. So we'll give him a bit of time and then we'll find another race for him, maybe back at Windsor. 02-07-25

runners.breeder: J P M Main & Andrew Knott
runners.comment: Latest effort shows he retains full ability aged eight; may remain competitive
runners.name: Mister Bluebird

quotes.race: Ascot Shop Handicap
quotes.quote: Mister Bluebird's dam won this race seven years ago and he is her only foal, so it's a good story. We wanted to see if he'd get this trip and Rossa [Ryan, jockey] felt this stiff six was just what he wanted. He was having a good look at the stand too. We'll wait for the handicapper and then see what we do next - Heather Main, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap
quotes.quote: Mister Bluebird was very straightforward last year and unlucky not to win. He got the job done today and I'm pleased for the horse. - William Buick, rider

runners.spotlight: Went close at Musselburgh (7f, good) last time, showing he retains full ability aged eight; dual winner at Goodwood and may remain competitive; gained last three wins on soft ground.

runners.comment: Best form at 7f on good/firmer; chance may depend on the actions of the weather
runners.name: Crimson Spirit

quotes.race: Star Sports We Believe In Bookmaking Handicap
quotes.quote: You haven't seen Crimson Spirit at his best there. He went to go and win his race and then got blown around a bit, got unbalanced and the second horse just lunged at him a bit. I thought he did well in difficult circumstances and it was more a case of job done than seeing what he could do - Richard Kingscote, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Crimson Spirit was always in a nice rhythm. He wasn't trying to run to freely early on. He got a nice flow through, found a little gap and picked up nicely. The ground was much nicer than at Nottingham. I was pleased with the way he took me down that hill. We should have some fun with him next year as well - Richard Kingscote, rider.

runners.spotlight: Best form at 7f on good/firmer; completed a hat-trick last summer and ran creditably in big field at Newmarket in the first of his two starts this term; chance may depend on the actions of the weather, however.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well on his reappearance at York. He's a lovely, big, scopey gelding with lots to look forward to as the season progresses. He handles any track, he's versatile and he's a fun horse who should be winning more races. We're looking at Salisbury for him on Sunday. 11-06-25

runners.comment: Unfavourable draw played a part in him failing to transfer AW form back to turf last time
runners.name: Shiplake
runners.spotlight: Record of 3-5 on AW includes two stylish wins over 7f at Southwell for new yard; unfavourable draw played a part in him failing to transfer the form back to turf in the Victoria Cup when admittedly taking record in this sphere to 0-6.

runners.comment: Not beaten entirely by 7.5f trip on reappearance but is still seeking first win beyond 6f
runners.name: Solar Aclaim
runners.spotlight: Didn't seem beaten entirely by the 7.5f trip at Chester on seasonal debut but is still seeking a first success beyond sprint distances; not exactly guaranteed to take advantage of being 1lb below last winning mark.

stable_tour.quote: He won well at Chester last time. He's useful on soft ground but is very ground dependent. He's in the Stewards' Cup but won't run unless the ground is right for him, so he's the opposite to Indian Run, who won't run if it's too soft. 23-07-25

runners.comment: Chance of doubling his tally largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear
runners.name: Al Arbeed
runners.spotlight: Has been unable to sustain early progress and is 0-7 since debut success; ran respectably on penultimate start and is on a reduced mark but chance of doubling his tally largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

stable_tour.quote: He'd have needed his first race of the season, but I was a bit disappointed with his next at Musselburgh. Perhaps the undulations didn't suit him, and he wasn't drawn all that well, so don't judge him on that because I think he'll make his mark in decent handicaps. I may put some headgear on him next time. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Form dipped returned to turf last time; hasn't scored in this sphere since his 2yo days
runners.name: The Dragon King

quotes.race: £150,000 Tattersalls October Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've seen it all now. I was working out what to tell the members at halfway when The Dragon King was last and going nowhere as it was going to be a long day, but what a ride by William. When you see a horse come with that rattle, you know they're going to get there. We like to buy this type of horse from the Somerville sale. He was a sensible purchase and Tattersalls have looked after the owners well here today. I think there is a Group 2 race we can supplement him for, but we'll have to celebrate this first - Middleham Park racing manager Tim Palin.

runners.spotlight: Previously effective on turf but form dipped returned to this sphere last time and he still hasn't scored on grass since his 2yo days; admittedly on a workable mark provided he rebounds.

stable_tour.quote: He had a really successful two-year-old season last year, winning three times, including the big sales race at Newmarket on his final run. He grew a little bit over the winter and we're pleased with what we're seeing. 17-04-25

runners.comment: Pair of duck eggs this term don't tell the whole story; record of 1211 over 7f previously
runners.name: Morte Point
runners.spotlight: Produced form figures of 1211 once upped to 7f last term; has posted two duck eggs this season but raced further back than usual on reappearance and was unfavourably drawn in the Victoria Cup latest; may prove resurgent.

runners.comment: Returns to his ideal sphere but brings a question mark over current form
runners.name: Lunario

prev_owners.owner: Michael Watt Roy David Christmas Party
Christmas Party M Watt & R David

runners.spotlight: Returns to his ideal sphere (turf) but brings a question mark over his current form, having trailed home last in both AW outings this year; possibly out of his depth to boot, having never won above Class 4.

runners.comment: Still needs to prove her best AW form can be transferred back to turf
runners.name: Fouette
runners.spotlight: Similar type to Shiplake, with still having to prove that best AW form can be transferred back to turf; not exactly solid on 2026 efforts anyway and doesn't look the percentage call in this competitive field.

runners.comment: Three duck eggs since 2024; needs to prove he retains ability; second run for new yard
runners.name: Metal Merchant

quotes.race: OLBG Spring Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: I was quietly confident Metal Merchant would run a nice race but in these big handicaps you can be on the wrong side and all sorts, but that was a very smart performance. He was a decent 2yo and 3yo but it wasn't until we gelded him that he really flourished. He's going to be a nice horse to go for those big mile handicaps -  Jack Channon, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing Welfare Classified Stakes
quotes.quote: Metal Merchant deserved that. He's a tough horse who has been at the top of his handicap mark all season. He loves his racing and takes it well but there might not be anything else for him this season. He'll be gelded over the winter and should be a nice horse for those big handicaps next season - Jack Channon, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Showed notable handicap form in 2024 but has posted duck eggs in three runs since that campaign and needs to prove he retains ability; best watched on second run for new yard, unless the market suggests otherwise.

stable_tour.quote: He won the Spring Cup at Newbury last year and ran some really creditable races in the top handicaps for the rest of the season. He seems to have come back from his winter break in good shape and he's training really well. We initially thought about the Lincoln, but I think we'll go back to Newbury for the Spring Cup again. He'll campaign in those big mile handicaps. He ran well for a long way in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot and all those types of races will be on his agenda. We hope he can pick up one of them. 02-04-25

runners.breeder: Airlie Stud & Mrs S M Rogers
runners.comment: Good spell around this time last year; possibilities if taking well to refitted blinkers
runners.name: Rare Change
runners.owner: Mrs J Woods And K Lawrence

quotes.race: Conundrum HR Consulting Handicap
quotes.quote: Rare Change threatened in nurseries last year to take himself to the next level and he's done that. He needed to today. We were markedly up in grade but did it really well. I thought it was very close but I was in the right place - Hector Crouch, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Had bad luck in running over C&D during an otherwise successful spell around this time last year; inconsistent since but has possibilities off current mark provided he takes to refitted blinkers (worn once previously, as a 2yo).

stable_tour.quote: We've always held him in high regard and he ran a blinder at Glorious Goodwood when third in a 6f nursery. Oisin Murphy felt he may have ridden him wrong on the day but he competed well in a very good nursery. He was only sixth at Doncaster last Friday, so he's frustrating, but talented, and we're going to have to figure out how to win with him. 18-09-24

runners.comment: On two-year losing spell but is on a very attractive mark and drops in class
runners.name: Seven Questions

quotes.race: William Hill Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: It's been a big team effort with this horse as he's as quirky as they come. Seven Questions spent the night at the racecourse last night as we know when he gets on the horsebox, he gets very stirred up. So, he had an away night about half a mile from his stable. We saddled him about an hour ago and brought him down - he was trying to kick everyone. He's a talented horse on his day and got a brilliant ride. We'll have to re-evaluate where we go now as he was very much at a crossroads. We'll have to see whether he is a Royal Ascot horse - George Scott, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; on a losing spell that goes back to Group 3 success two years ago but is on a very attractive mark and his Class 2 form this term includes a couple of respectable efforts; this combination of a drop in grade and assistance of Jamie Spencer (up for first time; regular jockey for the owner) may be the time to catch him.

stable_tour.quote: He ran an absolute blinder at Chester the other day when fourth behind Roman Dragon - he showed phenomenal speed from the inside gate, which he needed to do, and tanked along beautifully. I'm going to keep him quite busy - I think he's very well handicapped and if he does win a handicap - which I'm sure he will - he could then go on and win one or two quite cosily. He's frighteningly well handicapped and will be dangerous in any race he shows up in. He runs at Goodwood on Friday. 20-05-26

runners.comment: Won at Ripon on stable/seasonal debut and remains well treated on peak form
runners.name: Dream Composer

quotes.race: Ripon Silver Sprint Trophy Handicap
quotes.quote: The change in yards has helped freshen Dream Composer up. The race went to plan and I was told to kick early on him and he kept on galloping. I thought maybe I would get caught but he kept going - Myla Coppins, jockey.

quotes.race: Aston Martin "Dash" Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: We bought Dream Composer very inexpensively from France three years ago - he'd run as a 2yo there - and he's won for us every year. He keeps stepping up, and obviously this is the icing on the cake, winning one like this. He's won some good races at Grade One tracks; we just felt he was handicapped quite well today, and the cut in the ground helps him. He's pretty good at going up and down dale, because he's won at Goodwood and places like that. We were going along as we found it; he's got an entry in the Wokingham and if a penalty gets him into it and there's cut in the ground, he likes Ascot and has run well there, so that's a possible. But we'll enjoy today and see where it takes us - James Evans, trainer.

quotes.race: Cavani Menswear Sartorial Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: I think the ground was a bit too lively at Royal Ascot. Dream Composer has been travelling much better in his races so the five seems to suit well now. There is the five-furlong handicap on the first day of Glorious Goodwood which is a 0-105 and that was a thought, and obviously the Stewards' Cup would come into consideration as well - James Evans, trainer.

quotes.race: Peroni Nastro Azzurro Handicap
quotes.quote: Dream Composer has great form here and likes this ground, so everything was in our favour. The race went to plan and he keeps galloping. He probably likes 6f more than five, but the ground helped him - you might as well use his stamina over five - Mollie Phillips, rider.

runners.spotlight: Regained the winning thread at Ripon (5f, good) on stable/seasonal debut when 5lb lower and rider took off 7lb; this seems a harder task but he remains well treated on peak form and is a dual winner at Goodwood; enters calculations.

runners.comment: 0-7 for current yard but has two pieces of encouraging form this year; possibilities
runners.name: Dyonisos

prev_owners.owner: L Baudron Alessandro Botti Et Al

runners.spotlight: Ex-French 4yo who is 0-7 for current yard but has two pieces of encouraging form this year, namely placed efforts at Meydan and Newmarket on good ground (perhaps ideally suited by softer); below par last time but otherwise has possibilities.

runners.comment: Went close at Nottingham last time; again gets weight all round; may remain competitive
runners.name: Nogos Dream

quotes.race: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: There's a tailwind there so speed is more likely to carry on but Nogo's Dream is in great shape - Oisin Murphy, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Has registered two wins apiece on AW and turf; went close at Nottingham (5f, good) most recently; again receives weight all round and may well remain competitive; has bits of C&D form.

stable_tour.quote: Some people don't like him but I love him. If every horse in the yard was second nearly every time they ran you'd be happy. He's a bit quirky and we took all the gear off him for Sandown on Saturday, when he finished fourth after getting no luck in running. But that's Nogo, you have to ride him for luck and we didn't get it. He's ultra-consistent and it's just about finding the key to him. 18-09-24

runners.comment: Went close at Beverley on penultimate start; paid for racing freely in cheekpieces latest
runners.name: Canons House
runners.owner: M McHale J Munroe M Guy & D Walshe

prev_owners.owner: M McHale And J Munroe Racing

quotes.race: Saddle Room Deliciously Casual Cafe Dining Handicap
quotes.quote: We had a significant draw advantage and that really helped. Canon's House has done his best every day of his life. He always had a funny head carriage, but no one's complaining about that now. We can't work out why there's been such huge improvement, but we've got a day to find a race to run him in - David Easterby, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Andersons - Quality For The Home Handicap
quotes.quote: Canon's House showed plenty last year but things just didn't work out towards the back end. He's been in good form and this race has been the target. Hopefully he'll pick up another couple - Billy Garritty, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Did well last term, winning four times; went close at Beverley on penultimate start and paid for racing freely in cheekpieces a few days later; runs without the headgear this time and could go well.

runners.comment: Not disgraced back on turf last time but took his record in this sphere to 0-9
runners.name: Fidelius
runners.spotlight: Record of 6-17 on AW includes two wins in a consistent 2026 campaign; not disgraced back on turf last time but finished only fifth of six and took record in this sphere to 0-9; others preferred.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a wonderful winter - he's been absolutely superb with three wins and three seconds and has kept the flag flying for us. Although he hasn't won on the turf yet, he's had some good placed efforts. At the moment he just needs to bounce back from a run at Bath the other day that didn't really work out for him, but I think he'll be winning again and hopefully on the turf as well. 20-05-26

runners.comment: Needs to prove he can transfer AW form back to turf; mark has gone up in tandem
runners.name: Star Chorus
runners.spotlight: Prevailed in reapplied hood at Southwell (6f) last time, taking AW record to 4-13; needs to prove he can transfer the form back to turf; only 1-10 in this sphere and is 7lb higher than last attempt.

runners.comment: Weighted to the hilt on reappearance, being still on career-high mark
runners.name: Glamorous Breeze

quotes.race: S H Jones Wines Handicap
quotes.quote: Glamorous Breeze is just quirky. She's got plenty of ability and was second in a Listed race last season. This year I figured her out, sit, hold still then [go] last 50 yards. It's not she's ungenuine, she just does enough - William Cox, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Ended last season in good form on AW; has done most of her winning on turf but looks weighted to the hilt on reappearance, being still on a career-high mark; seems unlikely to improve aged eight.

runners.comment: Hindered by wide draw last time, otherwise has a good record over 5f
runners.name: Roach Power
runners.spotlight: Very productive in 2025, winning five times; hindered by wide draw at Chester most recently, otherwise has a good record over 5f; just needs to prove he can overcome current mark.

stable_tour.quote: He just needed the race first time out at Doncaster and he's in good form now. He's won over seven furlongs, but he's quick and is just as good at six furlongs. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Lacks recent match practice and remains on career-high mark
runners.name: Forager
runners.spotlight: Lacks recent match practice, remains on career-high mark and won't have her apparent ideal ground (good to firm) unless the weather lends her a big hand; not the percentage call.

13:45.race_name: Newsells Park Stud Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Inexperience evident when third on last month's debut; could have lots more to offer
runners.name: Fashions Fancy
runners.spotlight: Inexperience evident when 5l third of six at 10-1 behind odds-on stablemate on last month's debut at Kempton (1m3f, AW); from a classy family and could have lots more to offer for her leading yard; key player.

runners.comment: Well-bred Godolphin newcomer; leading trainer also saddles Kempton third Fashion's Fancy
runners.name: Tribal Queen
runners.spotlight: Third foal; Frankel half-sister to 1m2f/1m4f winner Spirited Style (including Listed); dam 1m/1m2f Group 1 winner; could have a big part to play on debut, especially if strong in the betting; leading trainer also saddles Kempton third Fashion's Fancy.

runners.comment: Promise on both starts and this Irish Oaks entry might not be far away
runners.name: Ladykirk
runners.spotlight: Kept on for promising second on debut at Yarmouth (1m, good to soft) last October and reappeared with 8l fifth of ten in strong novice at Sandown (1m2f, good) four weeks ago; entered in the Irish Oaks; might not be far away.

runners.comment: Stayed on for fourth on 7f AW debut last December; this longer trip should be a firm plus
runners.name: Nochebuena
runners.spotlight: 13-2 when staying on for 4l fourth of eight on debut at Kempton (7f, AW) last December; her dam was a 1m/1m2f Group 1 winner in Peru and the step up in trip should be a firm plus for this Study Of Man filly; chance.

runners.breeder: Kirtlington Park M Eves & Aga Khan Stud
runners.comment: 210,000euros yearling; shaped as though she would improve for debut run; one to consider
runners.name: Ceinture dOrion
runners.spotlight: 210,000euros yearling with an attractive pedigree; shaped as though she would improve for the run when fourth of seven at 9-2 on last month's debut at Wetherby (1m2f, good to firm) and she's one to consider.

runners.comment: In top hands but always behind when 20-1 for last month's debut at Nottingham
runners.name: Shadida
runners.spotlight: In top hands and her dam was a Listed winner; she's one to watch in the betting on this second start but she was always behind when 20-1 for last month's debut at Nottingham (8.3f, good) and dramatic improvement is needed.

14:20.race_name: Oakmere Homes Supporting Macmillan EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 450,000gns yearling whose top northern trainer has made another fine start with his 2yos
runners.name: Minzelle
runners.spotlight: 85,000euros foal, 450,000gns yearling; by Minzaal; third foal; closely related to winners Turn On The Jets (5f including 2yo; RPR 112) and Saratoga Special (5f Listed); dam 5f winner (103); represents powerful northern yard that has made another fine start with 2yos; firmly in calculations on debut.

runners.comment: Chester runner-up; takes on some very interesting newcomers but sets useful form standard
runners.name: Jazz Queen
runners.spotlight: Improved upon last month's debut sixth at Newmarket (5f, good) when going close at Chester (5.5f good) a fortnight ago, shaping as though she would be suited by today's extra yardage; takes on some very interesting newcomers but sets a useful form standard for them to aim at.

runners.comment: 400,000gns 2yo breeze-up buy; Newmarket trainer does well with his 2yos here
runners.name: Libertango
runners.spotlight: 130,000euros yearling, 400,000gns 2yo breeze-ups; first foal; dam unplaced 6f/1m 2yo in US, sister to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Aktabantay, half-sister to winners Baydar (smart 1m-1m2f) and Reina Madre (French 7f Group 3), out of 1m2f Listed winner; Newmarket trainer is 5-14 (36%) with his 2yos here; this No Nay Never newcomer could play a leading role.

runners.comment: £190,000 yearling; makes debut; trainer's last two 2yo runners here have both won
runners.name: Eshaa
runners.spotlight: £190,000 yearling; third foal; dam 7f/1m winner (including Swedish Listed), half-sister to two French winners out of 1m winner; has travelled from Lambourn for her debut and trainer's last two 2yo runners here have both won.

runners.breeder: Watership Down Stud And W S Farish Snr
runners.comment: Dam 6f winner (including 2yo/Group 2); likely to improve for this debut but could run well
runners.name: Royal Message
runners.owner: Lord Lloyd Webber & W S Farish
runners.spotlight: Second foal; No Nay Never half-sister to 7f AW winner Champion Again Ole (RPR 86); dam 6f winner (including 2yo/Group 2), from talented family; likely to improve for this debut run but could give good account.

runners.comment: Trainer has already unearthed some useful 2yos this year; one to be interested in on debut
runners.name: Sea Venture
runners.spotlight: 70,000gns yearling (150,000gns vendor 2yo breeze-ups); fifth foal; Sea The Stars sister to winners Layaleena (7f 2yo/1m; RPR 93) and Beccara Rose (1m; 86); well-bred dam once-raced (52); trainer has already unearthed some useful 2yos this season and she's one to be interested in on debut.

runners.comment: 155,000euros yearling with an attractive pedigree; one of two newcomers for the yard
runners.name: Bint Minzaal
runners.spotlight: 155,000euros yearling; eighth foal; Minzaal half-sister to four winners including Je Zous (1m/9.4f including 2yo/Group 3), I'll Have Another (7f-1m6f including 2yo; RPR 102) and Bucky Larson (7f/1m; 100); dam 10.6f winner (81); one of two newcomers for yard; could go well on debut; check betting.

runners.comment: 95,000gns yearling; sister to 6f 2yo/1m winner Shout; no surprise to see good run on debut
runners.name: Harlequin Gift
runners.spotlight: 95,000gns yearling; third foal; Advertise sister to 6f 2yo/1m winner Shout (RPR 105), half-sister to 7.3f/1m winner Port Erin (83); dam French 7f/7.5f winner (89), half-sister to 6f Group 2 winner Overdose; one of two debutantes for the stable; no surprise to see a good run; betting may guide.

runners.comment: Well beaten at 16-1 at Ascot recently and needs to be an entirely different proposition
runners.name: Resemblance
runners.spotlight: £45,000 yearling who has an attractive pedigree and is open to improvement on this second start; however, she was well beaten at 16-1 at Ascot (5f, good) a fortnight ago and needs to be an entirely different proposition.

runners.comment: Third foal; dam 8.6f AW winner (RPR 70); others newcomers make greater appeal on paper
runners.name: Profitability
runners.owner: Peter Onslow & Mr & Mrs Gary Middlebrook
runners.spotlight: By Profitable; third foal; dam 8.6f AW winner (RPR 70), half-sister to useful winners Real Force (5f-7.5f including 2yo) and Real Gain (1m-1m2f including 2yo); others newcomers make greater appeal on paper.

runners.comment: Newcomer; Sottsass half-sister to 10.6f AW winner (RPR 56); she may prefer a longer trip
runners.name: Aurora Valkyrie
runners.spotlight: 18,000euros yearling; third foal; half-sister to 10.6f AW winner Lord Talbot (RPR 56); unraced dam closely related to 1m6f Listed winner Arya Tara, out of 1m2f winner; this Sottsass newcomer may prefer a longer trip.

runners.comment: £15,000 2yo breeze-ups; half-sister to seven winners but she may be best watched on debut
runners.name: Trust In Far
runners.spotlight: 10,000euros yearling, £15,000 2yo breeze-ups; tenth foal; Blackbeard half-sister to seven winners notably Stone Of Destiny (5f-6f; RPR 109), Stone Tornado (1m Listed) and Illusionist (5f-6f including 2yo; 97); she may be best watched on debut.

14:55.race_name: British Stallion Studs EBF Cecil Frail Stakes (Listed Race)

runners.comment: Listed/Group 3 winner last August; near-miss in Listed race on reappearance; strong claims
runners.name: Rosy Affair
runners.spotlight: Listed winner at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) last August and followed up in Group 3 at Deauville (6f, soft) 13 days later; reappeared with near-miss in Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) and has strong claims.

stable_tour.quote: She performed much better in the second half of last year and we toyed with the idea of the Al Quoz Sprint in Dubai but decided to be patient. It was no surprise when she won a Group 3 in August and she's going to work back from midsummer targets. We'd love to get her to Royal Ascot and I'd imagine she'll start in a Listed race. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Listed/Group 3 winner last summer and she could improve for her recent return at Newmarket
runners.name: Sky Majesty

quotes.race: Tally-Ho Stud Irish EBF Ballyogan Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Sky Majesty is just really coming back to herself now. It's taken a while to get her back on that comeback trail, but she felt fantastic there and stepped in a lot quicker than I thought she would off a better pace than the last day. She's just really filling back into herself and getting back into gear. Obviously, they'll be looking to get some Group 1 form into her, I'm sure - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Sky Majesty is a lovely filly who enjoyed that bit of cut in the ground and was strongly through the last hundred [metres]. We didn't go overly hard early, I was expecting there to be a little more tempo given the fact the track bias has been so strong and that probably didn't suit her too well but the stiff finish and the slow ground really helped to see her to best effect - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Criterium de Maisons-Laffitte (Group 2) (2yo) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Christophe said Sky Majesty didn't relish the ground, but she handled it. She did really well and the second filly, whether or not she ran to her best I don't know, but she's got some very good form. I don't think she does a lot [when she gets to the front]. She won a nose in her maiden and then a neck in the Firth of Clyde, so it looks like the better the race, the further she wins - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Firth Of Clyde (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: She's good. She's taken a nice step forward. Sky Majesty picked up great when I asked and showed a great attitude when it mattered - Callum Rodriguez, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Listed/Group 3 wins at Naas last summer (6f, yielding/good) then unplaced in two Group 1s; underwhelming on recent return at Newmarket (6f, good to firm; behind two of these) but those who raced more prominently were favoured and she could improve for that run; versatile ground-wise; key player.

runners.comment: Some solid form in defeat in Listed races and she could be thereabouts
runners.name: Magic Basma

quotes.race: Racing TV EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: It wasn't too much of a shock. Kevin was pretty hopeful. He said to just take a lead on Magic Basma and see how we get on, and just make sure she enjoys her first day at school ? and she seems to have done that. There was a lot of unraced horses in there, but the Roger Varian horse was coming in with a nice bit of form and I was very happy with my filly - Jockey Oisin McSweeney, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: 0-10 since winning on debut in August 2024 but she ran well in Listed races last August/September (various ground) and did likewise when fourth of nine on reappearance at Newmarket three weeks ago (6f, good to firm; Rosy Affair about 2l ahead in second); could be thereabouts.

runners.comment: 7f Group 3 win in France last October but she's struggled there on both starts this season
runners.name: Half Sovereign

prev_owners.owner: Sas Logistics Contracts Ltd & E Burke

quotes.race: Emirates Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches (Group 1) (Fillies) (Turf)
quotes.quote: The trip was a doubt in my mind and that's been compounded by the ground. Half Sovereign travelled lovely turning in and I thought we were in with a squeak, but she just didn't get home - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs "Carrie Red" EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: The plan was to come here and then go for a valuable Tattersalls sales race [at Newmarket] as she's only got a very low weight because of her cost. Then there's a nice Listed fillies' race in France at the end of October. Because Half Sovereign only cost 12,000gns as a yearling, you're a little bit negative in your thoughts of her, but she's done nothing but improve with every run, so who knows where she'll end up - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Fillies' Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Half Sovereign is a big, rangy filly who will be better next year. She did that well considering the track and ground didn't really play to her strengths - James Cowley, assistant to Karl Burke.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Half Sovereign keeps improving and she's a big filly. I thought we got easily in front and I was pulling up as we got to the line. Karl's got plenty of ammunition and maybe a nursery is the way forward with her, but we'll see. I think she could be versatile with the trip - Sam James, jockey.

quotes.race: EBF Stallions Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was very pleased with the way Half Sovereign ran first time. She was green, missed the break over six furlongs, I was on my head the whole way and she came home really well. We expected her to do that today stepping up to seven and she'll even get a mile. She's a lovely big, strong filly who will probably get better as she gets older - Sam James, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: 5-7 in 2yo season, a campaign that culminated with Group 3 win at Chantilly (7f, very soft); the drop back in trip could be a positive but she's been well beaten on both starts this season, most recently in the French 1,000 Guineas; carries a 5lb penalty and a major turnaround is needed.

stable_tour.quote: Fetched a huge price at the sales and we're very grateful to Lady Bamford for sending her back to us. She was always a big, leggy two-year-old and she's gone forward physically and got stronger. She goes to Deauville on April 7 for a French Guineas trial [Prix Imprudence] and will go for the French Guineas if it all goes well. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Listed third at Ayr last September and she's not discounted back on slow ground
runners.name: Rhyme Dust
runners.spotlight: More than just not handling the track was amiss when she was last on her recent return at Newmarket (6f, good to firm); however, this lightly raced 4yo showed improved form when tackling soft ground at Ayr last September, finishing third in that 5.5f Listed race; not discounted back on slow ground.

runners.comment: Fourth in Group 2 Lowther last August but tailed off in Ayr Group 3 on soft when last seen
runners.name: Dandana

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I think Dandana was always doing enough. Every time one came to me she went on. I've always liked her - she's a nice filly who is a bit quirky. I don't think she enjoyed the track but she got through it. She'll become more straightforward and I'm sure she'll be fine stepping up a grade. She's done it the hard way and could be a stakes filly - Harry Davies, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Unibet/British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We discussed beforehand that we wouldn't want to be far away with Dandana. She's quite a nice filly but the surface is riding very slow and I probably could have done with a lead until the last furlong. She was having a good look around and ears pricked towards the line and I'm sure that whatever she's done today she'll improve on - Harry Davies, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Won last summer on first two starts (6f, AW/good) before respectable fourth in the Group 2 Lowther at York (6f, good to firm); however, tailed off in Group 3 Firth of Clyde at Ayr (6f, soft) in September and she has something to prove on the forecast slow ground on this reappearance.

runners.comment: 2-2; steep rise in grade today but it remains to be seen where her limitations lie
runners.name: Lady Youmzain

quotes.race: Constant Security Services Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lady Youmzain was always going to improve from two to three and she showed a great attitude carrying a penalty, which was always going to be tough. We'll see how she comes out of the race and discuss it with Mr Abdullah [owner] and representatives and see where we go from there - Adam Ryan, trainer's assistant, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Impressive at Beverley (5f, soft) last September on sole 2yo start and readily justified odds-on favouritism in four-runner Pontefract novice (6f, good) last month; this is a steep rise in grade but it remains to be seen where her limitations lie; she's one to consider.

runners.comment: Progressive 2yo last year; open to further improvement but it's very much necessary today
runners.name: Coconut Cove
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) last October and took another step forward when sixth of 19 in Listed race at Newmarket later that month (6f, good; unraced on softer); with a good trainer and she's open to further improvement, but it's very much necessary today.

stable_tour.quote: She's tidy and will probably start off in the Listed Chelmer Fillies' Stakes at Chelmsford over six furlongs. She went close to getting black type last season. If we can secure that this term, it will be deemed a successful year. 01-04-26

runners.comment: Not beaten far in the Fred Darling on reappearance; each-way chance back on slow ground
runners.name: Figjam
runners.spotlight: Ran four times in last year's 2yo campaign and best form came over 6f on soft/heavy ground, with a Group 3 fourth at Ayr and a Listed second at Doncaster; not beaten far when seventh of 14 at 66-1 on reappearance in the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good); each-way chance back on slow ground.

runners.comment: Kept on for fifth of 14 in Bath Listed race (5f); the return to 6f can suit; not ruled out
runners.name: Angel Shared

quotes.race: Clarke & Sons Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Angel Shared misbehaved on her debut here but still ran a cracker. She's had experience now and I wouldn't be surprised if she comes back next year even better - Dougie Costello, jockey, talking to RacingTV.

runners.spotlight: Completed 6f Newmarket handicap hat-trick last summer (good to firm); kept on well for fifth of 14 in Listed race at Bath (5f, good) last month and close third in handicap there (5f, good) latest; has run well on heavy ground here; improvement needed but the return to 6f can suit; not ruled out.

runners.comment: Went close in Group 3 at Newmarket last August but well beaten on both starts this spring
runners.name: Princess Petrol

quotes.race: British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was really smart. Princess Petrol had a lovely intro at Newbury with George Downing, who gave her a lovely educational ride, and learned a lot there. She's reaped the rewards here. There was a moment of worry in the stalls but she does that, even going to the stables sometimes. She likes to make everyone think she's in charge. We'll go 7f next time. Her dam won the Oh So Sharp Stakes and those kind of races would be good for her, but the Sweet Solera might come too soon. We'll definitely step up in class now - Ed Walker, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Went close in Group 3 Sweet Solera at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last August and again ran well when fourth of five in Group 2 at Longchamp (1m, soft) in September; however, well beaten in Group 3/Listed races (7f/6f, good) on her two starts this spring and has to get back on track.

stable_tour.quote: She did very well last year and was unlucky not to win the Sweet Solera Stakes at Newmarket. She hasn't progressed a great deal physically, but she's been training well and she was coming with a bit of a run on the toughest part of the track in the Fred Darling until she got knocked sideways. She was a bit gassy but hopefully that run has blown the cobwebs away. We'll probably go for a Listed race next and try to get that all-important stakes win. 22-04-26

runners.breeder: Airlie Stud & Mrs S M Rogers
runners.comment: Listed third at Newmarket last October but heavily beaten in Group 3 at Newbury on return
