runners.name: Splish Splash

quotes.race: CopyBet Acca Boost Up To 100% EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Splish Splash had run lovely but this was what we were expecting to see. She'll mature a lot over the winter and will stay further. She's one to look forward to - Charles Bishop, jockey.

runners.spotlight: All five starts on good ground; easily made all in C&D maiden last October on third outing and third of 19 in Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good) a fortnight later; she's much better than she showed on her reappearance at Newbury but was heavily beaten; others arrive with more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Solid profile in h'caps prior to a blip last time; up against it even if back to her best
runners.name: Lady Roxby
runners.spotlight: Steadily progressive in turf handicaps last season and reappeared with encouraging third at Kempton (6f, AW) last month; however, well beaten at Newmarket since and looks up against it today even if back to her best.

runners.breeder: Al Shaqab Racing & S N C Ecurie De Cast
runners.comment: Two-time winner in France but not at the top of her game in Britain this spring
runners.name: Paris Babe
runners.spotlight: Two-time winner in France, the latest last November; however, others have stronger form and she hasn't been at the top of her game this spring on her first two runs in Britain.

runners.comment: Exposed 6yo who goes up in grade this afternoon and would be a shock winner
runners.name: Powdering
runners.spotlight: Admirable 6yo who has won eight of her 52 starts (including on soft); however, she goes up in grade this afternoon and would be a shock winner.

runners.comment: Came up short in Listed race and two nurseries towards end of last season; hard to fancy
runners.name: Trust Amy

quotes.race: Nashville Soccer Club EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We quietly hoped Trust Amy would run well. We initially declared her in the seven-furlong handicap, but she'd have been topweight and on the softer ground we thought that would be a step too far. She's a lovely filly who shows plenty of speed, and we're pleasantly surprised by her. I'm absolutely delighted. Who knows where her ceiling is? It's very exciting for us. I don't think she needed to improve coming into today. Her Haydock run was nice and, although she was last at Chester, it was a better race and on quicker ground. It's nice to get her head in front and hopefully there's more to come - Gary Hanmer, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won Chester novice (6f, good to soft) last September on fourth run but came up short in Listed race and two nurseries subsequently; hard to fancy.

stable_tour.quote: A nice, sharp filly with plenty of pace who was bought from the breeze-ups a year ago. She looks good and is very exciting. She's settled down a lot from her two-year-old year. She's not over-big but she's a pocket rocket. She'll go to Chester as her owner Simon Boucher loves it there. We're looking for somewhere at the end of the month to get her started. 08-04-26

runners.comment: French AW conditions race winner for Amy Murphy; improvement needed on stable debut
runners.name: Thora
runners.spotlight: All five starts have been in France; won conditions race at Chantilly (6.5f, AW) last October and signed off for Amy Murphy with fifth of 13 in Listed race there (6.5f. AW) in March; improvement needed on stable debut (remains in same ownership).

15:30.race_name: Oakmere Homes Together For Macmillan EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Trainer is enjoying an excellent spring with his 2yos; could play a leading role on debut
runners.name: Pats Cash
runners.spotlight: 19,000gns foal, 55,000gns yearling; sixth foal; Perfect Power half-brother to US 5.5f-6.5f winner Philipsburg; dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Shadn, out of 7f Listed winner; trainer is enjoying an excellent spring with his 2yos and this one could play a leading role on debut.

runners.comment: Second on last week's debut (5.7f); mixed messages in pedigree regarding this sort of trip
runners.name: Tribal Appearance
runners.spotlight: 4-5 favourite when no match for the winner in second of five on last Wednesday's debut at Bath (5.7f, firm); there are mixed messages in his pedigree regarding the suitability of today's step up in trip but he's open to improvement and is entitled to respect.

runners.comment: Late headway on last week's debut over 5f at Salisbury and the step up to 7f may well suit
runners.name: The Bookkeeper
runners.spotlight: 10-1 and hampered leaving the stalls when fourth of six, beaten just over 5l, on last Thursday's debut at Salisbury (5f, good); he made some late headway and, with his dam being a 7f 2yo winner, he's open to improvement at this longer trip; interesting, all the more so if well backed.

runners.comment: There's plenty of potential in his pedigree and he could be a contender on debut
runners.name: Time For The Moon
runners.spotlight: 60,000gns yearling; 11th foal; Sea The Moon brother to 1m4f Australian Group 1 winner Durston, half-brother to four winners including Cubanita (1m-1m4f including 2yo/Group 3) and Aquarium (7f-1m2f; RPR 109); there's plenty of potential in his pedigree and he could be a contender on debut.

16:05.race_name: Oakmere Homes Racing For Macmillan Handicap

runners.comment: Two 1m2f wins on Lingfield AW this year but he accomplished little in his three turf races
runners.name: Joseph

quotes.race: Make The Move To Midnite Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a bit of a mess at the start but Joseph got into a lovely rhythm and he quickened up nicely. I thought the eventual second was going to keep going but he hauled them back and kept on well. It was his first try over a mile and a quarter but he was well up for it there - Donagh Murphy, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Off the mark in February, at the 16th attempt, and he narrowly justified favouritism last month as well; both of those races were over 1m2f but on Lingfield AW and he's accomplished little in his three turf races, the latest on penultimate start; others therefore look more solid.

runners.comment: Pretty reliable; second of 14 at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) in March last time
runners.name: Golspie
runners.spotlight: 1m2f wins last year at Pontefract (good) in June and Newcastle (AW) in December; pretty reliable and second of 14 at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) on return to turf in March showed again that he should be seriously involved.

stable_tour.quote: This colt made a winning start to his career when taking a mile maiden at Newbury, when I thought he had a good chance. Last time out I sent him to Newmarket for his handicap debut but the ground was too fast. When he won it was soft and we have learned that he must have plenty of give underfoot to be his best. I think he is on a nice mark (81) when the ground is right. 11-07-23

runners.comment: 5 races; first tongue-tie when winning at Kempton (1m, AW) last April by a head; off since
runners.name: Norflondonforever
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo who took a big step forward in first-time tongue-tie when landing a 1m handicap on Kempton AW last April by a head; that win was gained with a late challenge (sole attempt at 1m2f was debut) but he's been absent since, which probably poses the biggest question.

runners.comment: Struggled badly in four handicaps last term but reappeared with a closer finish (1m2f, AW)
runners.name: Blue Wonder
runners.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; struggled badly in her four handicaps last season but reappeared with a closer finish when fourth of ten at Lingfield (1m2f, AW; 16-1) late last month; needs to build on that.

stable_tour.quote: She's nice. She's been second twice and wasn't beaten far last time at Haydock behind Previse. She just needs the rub of the green to get her head in front and could go back to Haydock on Friday. 29-05-25

runners.comment: In good form last May-July; player if he can stay 1m2f, which isn't nailed on
runners.name: Bellasio
runners.spotlight: In good form last May-July, winning at Carlisle (1m, soft) and runner-up on four occasions, including there at 1m1f on soft; never dangerous on reappearance 15 days ago, which also happened at the same juncture last term before a good run next time; player if he can stay 1m2f, which isn't nailed on.

stable_tour.quote: We've always thought he was a talented horse and he's come back in great form after nearly a year off. He won at Carlisle in June and has finished second four times, which is very frustrating, but he's more than capable off his mark. Soft ground is pretty key so he's had a midsummer break in preparation for an autumn campaign running into the all-weather. He's got 10lb in hand if we can get him right on the day. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Won from front at Doncaster (1m2f, soft; 6lb higher today) in October; needs a second look
runners.name: Lesrico
runners.spotlight: Ninth start when off the mark in game fashion from the front at Doncaster (1m2f, soft; 6lb higher today) in October under Ben Ffrench Davis; out of the handicap when appearing to run well 11 days later (1m2f, good) and he needs a second look on this reappearance.

runners.comment: Best turf efforts when placed here but his three AW runs this spring were rather muted
runners.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners.spotlight: All three wins were on AW, at up to 1m3f; best turf efforts when placed at this track last August/September but his three AW runs this spring were rather muted; has career-low mark but needs to perk up.

runners.comment: The ground was softer than good for his 1m1f/1m2f wins last term; one to consider
runners.name: Hill O Rue
runners.owner: Gordon Bulloch & S Hardcastle D Szepler
runners.spotlight: Won handicaps last season when always prominent at Carlisle (1m1f, good to soft) in May and Beverley (1m2f, soft) in September; no show when 14-1 for reappearance one month ago, his first race on good to firm, but it's not hard to think he will be a lot more potent today.

runners.comment: Reappearance was probably a step back up the ladder; lacks any win for exactly two years
runners.name: Pol Roger
runners.spotlight: Lost his way in the autumn; has a favourable mark as a result and reappearance six weeks ago (without usual cheekpieces, which now return) was probably a step back up the ladder, but there's been no win for exactly two years.

stable_tour.quote: He went up 4lb to 74 after his last win at Ayr in May but then he's finished second in his last four races and has gone up another 7lb to 81. I'm thinking we need to change something and maybe try him over a bit further - he's been running over 1m2f - as he clearly looks to be in the handicapper's grip over that trip. 28-08-24

runners.comment: Reverts to 1m2f and probably okay on the ground, so he's considered each-way
runners.name: Imperial Trooper
runners.spotlight: Placed on three of five starts this year; wide draw no help at Chester two weeks ago when he had his first crack at 1m4f (tailed off); reverts to 1m2f and probably okay on the ground, so he's considered each-way.

runners.comment: Eight-race maiden who's not lived up to initial promise; up from 1m and stamina in family
runners.name: Give Me The Night
runners.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who has not lived up to initial promise; he's now 10lb lower than his opening mark but has not shown enough this term; moves up from 1m and there is stamina in the family.

runners.comment: Nine-race maiden who ended last term with two poor shows; left Brian Meehan for 15,000gns
runners.name: Dragonflame
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden who ended last term with two poor shows, with blinkers given a go on final outing; subsequently left Brian Meehan for 15,000gns in October; has a piece of 1m2f form, but below form on his only start on softer than good and non-runner for old yard when the ground was testing.

runners.comment: Veteran who is only 2-55 (last win 2022); well handicapped on some 1m6f form last season
runners.name: Red Derek
runners.spotlight: 10yo who's 2-55, with last win in 2022; well handicapped on some 1m6f form last term and probably needed recent run, but whether he can be competitive at this trip nowadays remains to be seen.

runners.comment: Big run is probably on its way after a promising 1m2f fourth at Sandown on handicap debut
runners.name: Bnaider
runners.spotlight: Third at Newbury (1m, soft) last October was his best form as 2yo and there was promise in his never-dangerous but staying-on fourth of six on handicap/seasonal debut at Sandown (1m2f, good; 6-1 from 8-1) four weeks ago; a big run is probably on its way.

runners.comment: Up 7lb for this turf debut but there was plenty to like about his Newcastle win (1m2f, AW)
runners.name: Central Command
runners.spotlight: Well held in three 7f AW runs late last year but second favourite with the visor enlisted for handicap/seasonal debut at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) three weeks ago, coming from towards rear to win comfortably in the end; up 7lb and makes turf debut but he has to be in serious calculations.

runners.comment: Won handicap/seasonal debut at Redcar (1m, good to firm) with a strong finish; up 7lb
runners.name: Ephron
runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Lxvi And P Demilow

quotes.race: Racing TV Club Day Here Today Handicap
quotes.quote: I was really pleased as I thought he'd need a bit more cut in the ground. Ephron has proven himself more versatile than I'd given him credit for. I'd been happy with his home work - Gemma Tutty, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 11-2 when seen in a very new light for handicap/seasonal debut at Redcar (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, coming from rear to win a nine-runner race by nearly 2l going away; 7lb higher but there was plenty of encouragement for 1m2f in that performance; one to consider.

stable_tour.quote: He won last week at Redcar on his first run in a handicap. He was very immature last year - his owners Middleham Park Racing were very patient with him and they got their rewards last week. His home work had been good but I wasn't that sure he'd be able to cope with the ground that fast, so it was very pleasing that he won. He looks like he'll stay 1m2f and he'd be a lot happier when there's more juice in the ground too, so hopefully there'll be a bit more to come from him. I'm looking forward to him for the rest of the season. 06-05-26

runners.comment: Best effort on debut but this is a new trip for handicap debut; with a powerful yard
runners.name: Oathbound
runners.spotlight: Fifth of ten at Newbury (1m, soft) in October on debut but he's not lived up to that promise in his two races since; admittedly 16-1 for last month's Wetherby reappearance (1m, good to firm) behind an odds-on stablemate; this is also a new trip for handicap debut, representing a powerful yard.

runners.comment: Won at Nottingham (1m, good); set a steady pace when trying 1m2f at Goodwood (good; 4th)
runners.name: Kokoluna
runners.spotlight: Big step forward on handicap debut when scoring at Nottingham (1m, good) last month; set a steady pace when trying 1m2f at Goodwood (good) three weeks ago, resulting in a creditable fourth of seven but she clearly needs to build on that.

runners.comment: Looked capable of better as 2yo; wind and gelding operations this spring; one to check out
runners.name: Lavender Gold
runners.owner: All For One Racing Ix & Chris Wright
runners.spotlight: Placed twice in the mud last September (made most on second occasion) before running on but never getting in a serious blow when 13-8 favourite for handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in November, still looking capable of better; had wind and gelding operations this spring; one to check out for a yard which had two notable well-backed winners last week.

runners.comment: Minor honours this term and 1m2f now looks in order (backed up by pedigree); place claims
runners.name: Dalamara
runners.spotlight: Finished well when scoring on handicap debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in December; ran creditably for minor honours in her two starts this season, over 1m on good and good to firm, after which 1m2f now looks in order (backed up by pedigree); place claims.

runners.comment: While not disgraced on handicap/turf debut (1m2f, good to firm), much better is needed
runners.name: Rumbustious
runners.spotlight: Staying-on third of six in maiden at Chelmsford (1m2f, AW) in March was best effort; while not disgraced when fourth of nine on handicap/turf debut at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) four weeks ago, much better is needed.

runners.comment: Returned to turf when tailed off at Newmarket (1m2f, good; 40-1) latest; caution advised
runners.name: Impossible Mission
runners.spotlight: Handicap debut winner at Wolverhampton (upped to 9.4f, AW) in November but ran poorly both starts since, returned to turf when tailed off at Newmarket (1m2f, good; 40-1) latest; down in class but caution advised.

runners.comment: Maybe he needed his stable/seasonal debut (25-1) but others have more pressing claims
runners.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners.spotlight: Seven races last year for David Loughnane and sole win in a Wolverhampton nursery (8.6f, AW) in October in first-time cheekpieces, which were kept when never dangerous in his two starts since; latest was stable/seasonal debut (25-1) and maybe he needed that run, but others have more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Faded when favourite for handicap/seasonal debut and latest run was a good deal worse
runners.name: Lady Hornblower
runners.spotlight: 7.4f Beverley maiden winner (good to firm; acts on soft) from four 2yo starts; faded when favourite for handicap/seasonal debut there in April and her Doncaster 1m run three weeks ago was a good deal worse, so she's best watched for the time being.

runners.breeder: Mount Coote Estates & R S Hoskins
runners.comment: Remote last of eight at Chester (1m4f, good; 80-1) on British debut 15 days ago
runners.name: Carwyn
runners.spotlight: Showed ability in two of his three maiden races in Ireland but well beaten on handicap debut there (1m) in October and a remote last of eight at Chester (1m4f, good; 80-1) on British debut 15 days ago; cheekpieces (worn for his last two Irish starts) return.

runners.comment: The first-time hood could help him settle; no ground issues; might be in with a chance
runners.name: Sagremor
runners.spotlight: Six-race maiden who tackles 1m for the first time and could do with settling better, but the first-time hood could help in that regard and he kept on when fifth of 11 at Lingfield (7f, AW) last time; effective on soft/heavy ground last year and he might be in with a chance.

runners.comment: Two backward steps since going close on debut; chance if tapping back into initial promise
runners.name: Sovereign Bay
runners.spotlight: All three starts over 1m on AW; runner-up on debut at Newcastle in February; two backward steps have followed but he could be a contender if tapping back into his initial promise on this handicap/turf debut.

runners.comment: Ran okay when fifth of 13 at the Curragh and this Irish raider could be in the shake-up
runners.name: Hambelton
runners.spotlight: 0-5 and yet to pose a serious threat but he ran fairly well from the front when fifth of 13 in a handicap at the Curragh (1m, soft) last month; he's travelled from Ireland to race today and could be in the shake-up.

runners.comment: Disappointing favourite last time but not ruled out given previous promise; handicap debut
runners.name: Blue Mantle
runners.spotlight: Disappointing favourite in Southwell novice (7f, AW) last month but short-headed in Newcastle maiden (7f, AW) previously; bred to be suited by this step up in trip and he's not ruled out on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Beaten a long way on reappearance but may have needed it; went close in his sole nursery
runners.name: Kiss For An Angel
runners.spotlight: Beaten a long way on reappearance at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) four weeks ago and it's hard to be confident on the back of that; however, he may have needed the run and he was a close second of five at Redcar (1m, good) last November in his sole nursery; a case can be made on that form.

runners.comment: No threat at Newmarket latest after a break but could have part to play back down in grade
runners.name: Senor Campanaro
runners.spotlight: Reared at the start and couldn't get into it at Newmarket (7f, good) last month when back from a break; won a four-runner nursery at Newcastle (7f, AW) in December on his first run since being gelded and he drops back in grade today; could have a part to play.

stable_tour.quote: He eventually broke his maiden in a nursery at Newcastle in December and has done well from two to three. The Rowley Mile course didn't suit him on his return and he'll be better on a more conventional track. He'll stay a bit further and should progress. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Won nicely at Wolverhampton in March; soundly beaten in midfield at Kempton on Wednesday
runners.name: Quick Turn
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the seventh attempt with an improved performance at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in March; did it nicely on that occasion but he was soundly beaten in mid-division at Kempton (1m, AW) on Wednesday.

runners.comment: Hasn't shone this spring but the drop back in trip and return to slower ground may help
runners.name: Alkumatic Jo Jo
runners.spotlight: Promising third at Bath (1m, soft) last October on second start and runner-up in Newcastle nursery (7f, AW) next time; she hasn't shone on her two runs this spring (1m/1m2f, good/good to firm) but the drop back in trip and return to slower ground may help.

runners.comment: Six-race maiden who is starting to look exposed; can be headstrong and goes up in trip
runners.name: Yorkshire Queen
runners.spotlight: She ran okay when fourth of 11 behind a comfortable winner at Southwell (7f, AW) a fortnight ago on reappearance; however, this six-race maiden is starting to look exposed and she can be headstrong, which is a concern on this first crack at 1m.

stable_tour.quote: She made a good start last week. I felt she was the best horse in the race despite not winning. We may pull her back to 6f next time, but equally she's all right over seven as long as it's not too stiff. We're going to try to win a maiden and then go to the restricted series final at Goodwood, which we won last year with Love Talk. She's a nice filly who will be better again next year. 04-09-25

runners.comment: 200-1 fourth at Kempton last month and he's one to consider on this handicap debut
runners.name: Claytons Kolatonic
runners.spotlight: Made debut in February and his three starts have been on AW; improved form when fourth of 13 at 200-1 over 1m at Kempton last month, behind three useful opponents; one to consider on handicap debut.

runners.comment: 0-6 at up to 7f and yet to finish better than fourth but has hinted 1m will be a good fit
runners.name: Jungle Knight
runners.spotlight: Six-race maiden who is yet to finish better than fourth but there were hints of promise in 7f nurseries here (good/good to soft; unraced on softer) last September and the way he kept on when mid-division on his recent reappearance at Southwell (7f, AW) suggests 1m could be a good fit.

runners.comment: 13 races and has won just once (last May) but this first crack at 1m is worth a go
runners.name: Paroda Diva

prev_owners.owner: Mps Racing Ltd Roger Thompson & Partner
Mps Racing Ltd Roger Thompson & Partner
Mps Racing Ltd Roger Thompson & Partner

runners.spotlight: She's raced 13 times and won just once (last May); also unproven on slow ground; however, she kept on galloping when sixth of 11 over 7f at Newmarket three weeks ago and this first crack at 1m is worth a go.

14:08.race_name: Download The Fairplay App Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners.breeder: Mountain View Stud & J C B/Stock
runners.comment: 1m6f seemed the best fit last year; perhaps in need of the race on return four weeks ago
runners.name: Captain Brett
runners.spotlight: 1m6f seemed the best fit last year, including for a win at Yarmouth (good) in June and also when first past the post at this track (firm; demoted after bumping) in July; perhaps in need of the race when last of five on return four weeks ago and he needs a second look back here.

runners.comment: Won here (11.5f, firm) nine days ago, leading over 1f out for a 5l win in six-runner race
runners.name: Basilette
runners.spotlight: Bumper/hurdles winner who's had another crack at the Flat on last two outings and scored here (11.5f, firm) nine days ago, leading over 1f out for a 5l win in six-runner race; penalty leaves her 3lb well-in compared to future handicaps and she's one for the shortlist.

stable_tour.quote: She's on a winter break. She's a summer filly - she won two hurdle races in October and loves Stratford for some reason. Her Flat handicap mark is very low (49), so when she comes back into training in February we'll wait until the ground has good, or even good to firm in it, and then she will mix and match Flat and hurdling for the summer. 21-01-26

runners.comment: AW classified winner who  has some turf form in the bumper and hurdle spheres
runners.name: Everest
runners.owner: Alan Jamieson Site Services & G L Moore
runners.spotlight: 17 races, finishing well in a 1m4f classified at Lingfield (AW) in March for her only win; second there off today's mark at same track (2m) last time was her best form under Flat rules and she has some turf form in the bumper and hurdle spheres; not entirely ruled out on Flat turf debut.

stable_tour.quote: We like this mare and she could be a nice prospect. We thought we'd go to Southwell in June and win but couldn't believe the depth of the race at that time of year. She hadn't been hard pressed for that and in the end found one too good but it was a promising run. She ran a nice enough race at Cheltenham on Saturday for her first run back and we'll try to find another bumper for her. She'll possibly go back to Cheltenham for the Paddy Power meeting. 29-10-24

runners.comment: 2lb below last winning mark; two respectable shows this term; one to take seriously
runners.name: Cloudy Rose
runners.spotlight: Had 1m4f and 1m6f wins on consecutive starts last summer and she's now 2lb below her last winning mark; following two respectable shows over 1m4f this term, she is one to take seriously on this return to 1m6f.

runners.comment: New trip might offer hope on first run since 18,000gns sale (left H Charlton) in October
runners.name: Big Win
runners.spotlight: Upped in trip and 11-10 favourite when weakening into third of six on handicap debut at Southwell (2m, AW) in September but that is the best form from his five starts; has otherwise not gone beyond 1m4f (tried in cheekpieces on final outing) so today's new trip might offer hope on this first run since 18,000gns sale out of Harry Charlton's last October.

runners.comment: Veteran whose two 2025 wins were at this track; last week's hurdles run was disappointing
runners.name: Man Of The Sea

quotes.race: NB Surfacing Handicap
quotes.quote: Man Of The Sea won well. Mr Mulholland said before the race he was in great form. He was a bit outpaced the last day at Windsor but he stays all day. He pinged the gates, I kept hold of him and he ran all the way to the line - George Rooke, rider.

quotes.race: Come Racing 11th November Nursery Handicap (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Man Of The Sea jumped and travelled, I was able to sit off the good pace and when I got stuck into him he saw it out to the line. He has plenty of experience and it stood to him. He did it well and hopefully there's another day in him - Billy Lee, rider

runners.spotlight: Veteran whose two 2025 wins were at this track over 1m6f and 1m5f; placed twice over hurdles last November but last week's run in that sphere (after a Flat reappearance here) was disappointing and dents his appeal.

runners.comment: Won twice on fast ground last May; recent reappearance was a step back in right direction
runners.name: Two Plus Two
runners.spotlight: Won on fast ground last May at Salisbury (1m6f) and Bath (11.5f); tailed off later that month but his recent reappearance here was a step back in the right direction; each-way claims if he's come on from that run.

runners.comment: Off the boil January-March and no revival 15 days ago; a major player if back on song
runners.name: Zooks
runners.spotlight: 37 starts, with her only wins coming last year on AW in February and at Ffos Las (1m6f, good) in July; went off the boil this January-March and no revival 15 days ago, after a break, but she'd be a major player if back on song.

runners.comment: Below form lately; raced freely when behind here on sole go beyond 1m4f (1m5f last year)
runners.name: Buck Barrow
runners.spotlight: Sole win (19 starts) was over 1m2f at Ffos Las last June; has the same mark today, having finished no better than sixth in his four races since, two of them this season; raced freely when behind here on his only attempt beyond 1m4f (1m5f last September) so there are enough doubts.

runners.comment: Has not come up to scratch at 1m4f-2m1f in her four handicaps, first three for M Tregoning
runners.name: Assured
runners.spotlight: Has not come up to scratch over 1m4f-2m1f in her four handicaps (trained last year by Marcus Tregoning, 2026 reappearance with this yard) and two of those were at this track, but she has fallen 9lb in the process.

14:43.race_name: MJ Church Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Blinkered for Lingfield debut (1m2f, AW) but won; the clear form pick and should improve
runners.name: Madrisa

quotes.race: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Madrisa has been a bit tricky at home but she has got a lot of ability and she's just learning, today was just about seeing where we are with her. I got a nice lead off Rab [Havlin, rider of the fourth] but when I pulled her out going coming down the dip she got a bit unbalanced but, when I gave her a tap to put the race to bed, she did it nicely - Cieren Fallon, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: By Decorated Knight; first foal of an unraced half-sister to dual 1m2f Group 3 winner Extra Elusive and the yard's Group 2 Gimcrack winner Ajaya; 10-1 and blinkered for debut in 12-runner maiden at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) late last month but she was always close up and kept on stoutly to lead in the final strides; the clear form pick in this field and should improve.

runners.comment: 5-6 for workmanlike novice win at Lingfield (1m, AW) in December; bred more for this trip
runners.name: Supplicate
runners.spotlight: Showed promise on debut last October and justified 5-6 favouritism in 12-runner novice at Lingfield (again 1m on AW) in December; the latter was in workmanlike style but she's bred more for this trip and is open to further improvement, which is needed.

runners.comment: 2nd of eight to impressive red-hot favourite in a novice at Kempton (1m3f, AW) 16 days ago
runners.name: Eloquencia
runners.spotlight: Modest form in a small field at Newmarket (7f, good) in April but second of eight to an impressive red-hot favourite in novice at Kempton (1m3f, AW) three weeks later; similar form to most of these and could improve again.

runners.comment: Madrisa was 8l ahead at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) last time and reopposes; major work to do
runners.name: Last Flight
runners.spotlight: 50-1 when never-dangerous seventh of 12 in maiden at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) last month, which was better than her December debut but winner Madrisa was 8l ahead at Lingfield and reopposes; major work to do despite revised terms.

runners.comment: Finished behind two of these rivals when 12-1 in a maiden at Lingfield (1m2f, AW
runners.name: Spinney
runners.spotlight: Dam useful at 1m2f-1m4f but this daughter was a 1,000gns yearling and finished behind two of these rivals when 12-1 in a maiden at Lingfield (1m2f, AW).

runners.comment: Showed little when 25-1 in a novice at Yarmouth (11.5f, good to firm) one month ago
runners.name: Clarissa Eclipse
runners.spotlight: Interesting on pedigree but she showed little when 25-1 in a five-runner novice at Yarmouth (11.5f, good to firm) one month ago.

runners.comment: No worthwhile form in a bumper, a 1m novice or a 1m2f maiden
runners.name: West Hill Rosie
runners.spotlight: No worthwhile form in a bumper, a 1m novice or when behind three of today's rivals in a 1m2f maiden.

15:18.race_name: Wiltshire And Bath Air Ambulance Raceday 15th July British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Raced front rank when third at Newbury and second at Newmarket; latter sets high standard
runners.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners.spotlight: Third of nine in a maiden at Newbury (5f, good) 16 days before her second of seven in a novice at Newmarket (5f, good to firm); raced front rank on both occasions and sets a high standard on the latter form.

runners.comment: £180,000 breeze-up 2yo; bred for speed and the stable's 2yos have made an impact this term
runners.name: Flight Signal
runners.spotlight: 82,000gns foal, £180,000 breeze-up 2yo; fourth foal; Mehmas half-brother to 6f/7f winner Thurso (RPR 83); dam 5f winner (including Listed; 95), half-sister to a useful 5f/5.5f winner and out of Italian 5f Listed winner; bred for speed and the stable's 2yos have already made an impact this term.

runners.comment: 80,000euros yearling, £140,000 breeze-up 2yo by Minzaal; needs to be good in this field
runners.name: Minkaas
runners.spotlight: 80,000euros yearling, £140,000 breeze-up 2yo; third foal; Minzaal half-sister to 5.5f/6f winner Spiritualism (including 2yo; RPR 74); dam 7f winner (68), half-sister to 7f 2yo Group 2 winner/1,000 Guineas runner-up Lucida, out of half-sister to Breeders' Cup Turf winner English Channel; first 2yo of the season for her stable and she needs to be good.

runners.comment: 5th of ten at Chester (5,5f, good) latest, showing plenty of speed in face of widest draw
runners.name: Paper View
runners.spotlight: Unable to justify favouritism over C&D (good) on debut; fifth of ten in maiden at Chester (5.5f, good) over four weeks later was better form, showing plenty of speed in the face of the widest draw; bold show seems likely but Jaan Ki Tikri looks a tough rival.

runners.comment: Made most when third of six at Salisbury (5f, good) but others in this have shown more
runners.name: On The Queue Tee
runners.spotlight: Dam US 5.5f turf 2yo winner; this daughter made most when third of six in a maiden at Salisbury (5f, good) eight days ago, despite starting 80-1, but two others in today's race have shown more.

runners.comment: Triple course winner who has finished close up here in her last two runs; respected
runners.name: Moes Legacy
runners.spotlight: Triple course winner who scored at Wolverhampton in March and she's gone close back at this track (5f/5,6f, firm) in last two runs; only 1lb higher than for her runner-up effort three weeks ago and she should make another bold bid.

runners.comment: All three wins have been on AW but she's been knocking on the door here in last two starts
runners.name: Toolatetonegotiate
runners.spotlight: All three wins have been on AW but she's been knocking on door here (5f, firm/good) in last two starts; nudged up 2lb but she's been as good as ever in her last two runs and should be in the thick of things again.

runners.breeder: W H & Mrs J I Simpson
runners.comment: Scored here in final 3yo run and she started this season with another C&D win; key player
runners.name: Silver Wraith

quotes.race: Bet Now With fairplaybet.co.uk Handicap
quotes.quote: Silver Wraith doesn't have much of a knee action so it was always ground that she should handle alright. Emma Lavelle talking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Scored here in (good to soft) in her final 3yo run and she started this campaign with another brave win over C&D (firm) last month; that took her Bath record to 2-2 and she's remains feasibly treated off only 2lb higher; key player.

runners.comment: Disappointing on Newmarket reappearance and she needs to bounce back near best
runners.name: Cuban Lady
runners.spotlight: Clearcut winner of a Windsor novice (6f, good to firm) last June; finished close up in three of her four handicaps last season but she reappeared with a 12l defeat at Newmarket (100-30) three weeks ago; that was in a Class 3 after six months off but she needs to bounce back after that disappointing run.

runners.comment: Four-time AW winner but she's 0-11 on turf and has been quiet in both runs this season
runners.name: Queue Dos
runners.spotlight: All four wins have been on AW and she's 0-11 on turf; finished placed a few times on good or quicker ground last summer but she's been quiet in both runs this season and others are more persuasive.

stable_tour.quote: She's for the same owners as Queues Likely and I think she's going to be very good. I think she'll definitely end up a black-type filly, most likely over a mile or seven furlongs. I was pleased with the way she ran at Bath because I thought she'd run a nice race as she'd been working lovely at home. Her half-brother was second in the Brocklesby and was sold to America straight away after that. He has run well in a big race in America and it's going to end up quite a nice page. She's got the size and scope. 04-07-24

runners.breeder: Mrs Mary Taylor And James F Taylor
runners.comment: Triple turf winner but she's been out of sorts in two runs for new yard this season
runners.name: Seraphim Angel

quotes.race: CAA Stellar Lily Agnes EBF Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Seraphim Angel went to Newmarket and didn't know what to do when she came off the bridle, but she had clearly learned a lot today. She's got lots of speed and I'd suggest she'd go to York for the Marygate - Tom Dascombe, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Triple turf winner who scored at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last July in her final run for Tom Dascombe; only 1lb higher than for that success but she's been out of sorts in two runs for new yard this spring and needs to get back on track.

runners.comment: Catterick winner who is still unexposed and needs a close look on handicap/seasonal debut
runners.name: Control Room
runners.spotlight: Unexposed filly who made all when landing a Catterick maiden (5f, soft; 7-2) last October; that was a very narrow success but she looks on a fair opening mark and should have more to offer as a 3yo; respected on handicap/seasonal debut

stable_tour.quote: She won at Catterick on her final start of last season. She did her final piece of work the other day and worked very nicely. runners.name: Too Many Spirits

runners.comment: Second at Hamilton last week (6f, good); open to further progress; high on the list
runners.name: Ricky Punting
runners.spotlight: Promise at Bath on debut and again when plugging on for second at Hamilton last week (6f, good); remains capable of better and he's high on the list.

runners.breeder: J A Knox And Mrs M A Knox
runners.comment: Green when fifth of nine on his Kempton debut 18 days ago; could take a big step forward
runners.name: Green Sovereign
runners.spotlight: Promise amidst inexperience when fifth of nine on his Kempton debut (6f, AW) 18 days ago; well drawn and could take a big step forward.

runners.comment: Good late headway to take third at Lingfield (6f, AW) three weeks ago; open to improvement
runners.name: Adoramus
runners.owner: Mr And Mrs R Everist And Partner
runners.spotlight: 12-1 for his Lingfield debut three weeks ago (6f, AW), a race where he kept on stealthily to take third; open to plenty of improvement but it will be needed.

runners.comment: 52,000gns half-brother to six winners (including Group 3); likely type on breeding
runners.name: Le Grand Etoile
runners.spotlight: 17,000euros foal, 52,000gns yearling; ninth foal; half-brother to six winners including Zannda (1m2f-1m4f including Group 3; RPR 103), Zanndabad (1m1f-10.5f Flat including 2yo, 101; useful 2m4f-2m6f hurdle) and Zenya (1m2f; 88); dam 1m4f AW winner (75); enough paper appeal to enter calculations.

runners.comment: Unplaced in two 5f runs; should be suited by 6f but improvement is essential
runners.name: Arrbob
runners.spotlight: His two runs over 5f suggest this longer trip will suit; can do better but he will need a good deal more to win.

runners.comment: 20,000gns half-brother to six winners; yard 0-8 (all unplaced) with 2yos this year
runners.name: Real Edition
runners.spotlight: 20,000gns yearling; eighth foal; half-brother to six winners including Real Force (5f-7.5f including 2yo; RPR 109), Real Gain (1m-1m2f including 2yo/AW; 107), Av A Word (1m2f; 75) and Hic Bibi (5.5f-7f; including 2yo/AW; 70); dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Camargo; likely type on paper but stable 0-8 (none placed) with 2yos this year.

runners.comment: 6,000euros half-brother to five winners out of an 8.5f winner; yard 0-8 with 2yos in 2026
runners.name: Fasthope
runners.spotlight: 5,000euros foal, 6,000euros yearling; eleventh foal; half-brother to five winners including Tamadhor (7f including 2yo; RPR 104), Bawaasil (7f/1m; 89), Madroos (1m; 83) and Alnaas (7f AW; 81); dam 8.5f winner (86), half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Memory; stable yet to hit the target with 2yos this year (0-8).

runners.comment: Only minor appeal on paper and yard's newcomers tend to be better for a run
runners.name: College Boy
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal of an unraced half-sister to useful US 1m-1m1f winner Maximova; stable's newcomers usually better for their debut.

runners.comment: 70,000euros close relation of 6f 2yo winner French Affair (RPR 78); yard 3% with turf 2yos
runners.name: Mr Minz
runners.spotlight: 70,000euros yearling; second foal; closely related to 6f 2yo winner French Affair (RPR 78); dam a modest four-race maiden (64); stable's 3% strike-rate with turf 2yos in the last five seasons tempers enthusiasm.

runners.comment: Two wins, including C&D, and a second from three runs this year; respected despite draw
runners.name: Betweenthesticks
runners.owner: J A Swinburne & Mrs Ruth A Carr
runners.spotlight: He has returned from a six-month break in rude health, winning at Wolverhampton and over C&D (second C&D success) last month and running well in his hat-trick bid at Ripon a fortnight ago; wide draw not ideal for a front-runner but he isn't handicapped out of things; trainer also runs Jojo Rabbit.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a really good buy, winning three times and being placed on four other occasions last season. He's been really fun for his owners. He's genuine and straightforward. He'll go to Pontefract or Wolverhampton on April 21. He can be competitive off his current handicap mark. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Conditions no problem and he went close off this mark at Beverley ten days ago; well drawn
runners.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners.owner: Grange Park Racing XIII & Ruth Carr

quotes.race: Watch Royal Ascot On Sky Sports Racing Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Jojo Rabbit got a nice lead this time rather than at Lingfield where he made the running and got hassled out of it. He's a nice type - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Made all to win a Class 6 handicap over C&D last month; not so good on his next two starts but returned to his recent best when a close second at Beverley ten days ago; runs off the same mark today and he's ideally drawn to attack; should go well.

stable_tour.quote: He has won nine races in total and seven for us, the latest at Pontefract last week. He's been a really fun horse for the syndicate that owns him as he gets out and about plenty. He's better with a bit of dig in the ground these days. He's well able off the handicap mark he's got at the moment, so hopefully he can go in again this season. He did it nicely at Pontefract. He has an entry at Wolverhampton on Friday, just in case we can run him well in at the weights and ahead of the handicapper. 15-04-26

runners.comment: On a losing run but on a dangerous mark and he can't be ruled out from a handy draw
runners.name: Knicks

prev_owners.owner: Capla Development J Nordoff L Westwood

quotes.race: tote.co.uk Saddle-Up For More Than Racing Handicap
quotes.quote: We didn't give Joanna any instructions, we just wanted to see what the drop back was going to do and it seems to have worked. It's Epsom next next, that's the plan - the three-year-old only Dash, because it's easier to win! - David Easterby, joint-trainer of Knicks.

runners.spotlight: Over two years since the second of his two wins; lurks on a dangerous mark though and his two runs this year have seen him finish within 3l of the winner; has his first run at Pontefract but he is effective around a left-hand turn; can't rule out from a handy draw.

runners.comment: 17th time lucky when winning at Catterick last month; 5lb rise might find him out
runners.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners.owner: John Kelly John McNeill & Kevin Mowatt
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the 17th attempt when leading late at Catterick last month (5f, good); beat a subsequent winner on that occasion but a 5lb rise might prove beyond him.

runners.comment: Four-time C&D winner, including this race in 2024; stall 10 dents confidence today
runners.name: Ventura Express

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now Handicap
quotes.quote: Ventura Express jumped a little bit slow but he soon travelled well through the race and he picked up and won nicely. I thought he would run well but I didn't quite expect that. He's been gelded which makes a massive difference because I don't think there's much else different than what Richard Fahey does, they're a lot better than us! - Paul Midgley, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Four of his six wins have come over C&D, including the corresponding race in 2024; drew a blank in 2025 but retains ability and he has run some solid races in defeat this year too, keeping on for fourth at Beverley 18 days ago; drops in class but he has the widest stall to contend with.

stable_tour.quote: He's been fantastic for us. He pays his way and is worth his weight in gold. The ideal scenario for him is a stiff 5f with an end-to-end gallop. He just failed last time at Pontefract, where they didn't go much of a pace. 14-08-25

runners.comment: Not at his best back on turf last month but he has often run well at this track
runners.name: Kings Crown
runners.spotlight: Two AW wins this winter; never in the hunt at Wetherby last month on his return to turf but he is effective over C&D and seems to handle any ground; not ruled out.

stable_tour.quote: We got him earlier this season from Adrian Nicholls. He was highly tried at two and three and has now dropped to what is a good handicap mark. He started the season on 72 and is down to 62 now. When he puts it together I can't believe he won't be winning soon. He'd be my dark horse. 28-08-24

runners.comment: Impressed in 1st-time visor (5f, AW) in December; many good runs since; needs more to win
runners.name: Ay Gee Ell
runners.spotlight: Blitzed his rivals at Southwell in December (5f) when a visor was first used; generally run well in defeat since but he will need to pull out more to take this prize.

runners.comment: Beaten 17 times since winning first two starts; drops in class on ground that should suit
runners.name: Changeofmind

quotes.race: British EBF 40th Anniversary Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Changeofmind is very exciting and one we rate a lot at home. He has lots of ability and natural talent. He'll go for the Westow Stakes next month at the Dante meeting. We'll take it one step at a time and keep our feet on the ground - Declan Carroll, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won his first two starts but beaten 17 times since; down the field at Thirsk on last week's reappearance but drops in grade today and the slower ground should suit.

runners.comment: Missed out by a short-head over C&D last month; draw excuse latest; stable runs two here
runners.name: Fuji Mountain
runners.spotlight: Won twice at Chester as a 2yo; just missed out over C&D last month (blinkers first time) when finding only Betweenthesticks too strong; ran okay at Beverley next time and he was drawn wide when disappointing back there ten days ago; stable also run Changeofmind.

runners.comment: Two 6f wins last summer, the second of them off this mark; needs to build on recent return
runners.name: Mrs Trump
runners.owner: R Chapman G J Daly & R J Parks
runners.spotlight: Last summer's two wins came over 6f, the second of them off this mark; should come on for her recent return to action but others appeal more for win purposes.

stable_tour.quote: What she lacks in ability, she makes up for in heart. She's very honest and genuine. She always does her best and she's done fantastically, winning three last year and a couple this time. She needs a flat 6f - she gets outpaced over 5f and runs out of track. 14-08-25

19:52.race_name: Thank You Alexia And Good Luck Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: 2-2 since cheekpieces went on; unpenalised for Sunday's Ripon win; drying ground will help
runners.name: Trojan Soldier

quotes.race: Anglo Stainless Supporting Yorkshire Wooden Spoon Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: Trojan Soldier takes a lot of stoking up and beforehand I spoke to his regular rider Jack Garritty, who said don't be afraid to kick on with three or furlongs to go as he takes a while to get into top gear. Once I found myself in that pocket on the rail, I knew I wasn't going to get out, so I had to hope the gap came. When it did, he was very brave to go into it as it wasn't that big, and he hit the line strongly - Jack Nicholls, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Improved for a step up in trip and then cheekpieces, getting off the mark at Southwell (1m6f) last month and following up at Ripon on Sunday (2m, good); escapes a penalty for that win and today's further rise in distance could spark additional progress; possible he could do with the ground drying out a bit but he's on the up and should make a bold bid to complete his hat-trick.

runners.comment: 0-6 but he has shown a good level of ability; new trip/headgear could prompt improvement
runners.name: Sea Of Kings
runners.spotlight: 0-6 but he has recorded an RPR of 84 or more in each of his last five starts; beaten at odds-on at Doncaster on his reappearance (1m4f, good to firm) four weeks ago; stepping up to a marathon trip could prompt further progress, as could the new cheekpieces; shortlisted.

runners.comment: 2m2f winner here last October; unexposed and he's an interesting contender
runners.name: Action Pact
runners.spotlight: Improved as his stamina was drawn out last season, winning over 2m2f here in October (soft); below par on extremely deep ground at Nottingham when last seen 211 days ago but that is not the run to judge him on; unlikely he has reached his ceiling and he's an interesting contender.

runners.comment: 3rd on last two starts but he has 3.75l to find with Trojan Soldier on Sunday's Ripon run
runners.name: Vaguely Royal

quotes.race: Five-Rivers Fostering Doncaster Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Vaguely Royal at Chepstow last time, we made the running and a combination of him still being green and getting lonely in front cost us the race. We were very confident coming here today, I just wanted to make sure I got a lead. William was going pretty steady in front, I wound him up in plenty of time but he won cosily. He's not a slow horse and I wouldn't see him getting much further than a mile and a half - Kieran Shoemark, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Comes here on the back of two third-place finishes but the latest was behind Trojan Soldier and there is no obvious reason why the placings would be reversed.

runners.comment: Won a chase on stable debut in November; well held on last month's return to the Flat
runners.name: Maghlaak

quotes.race: William Hill More Top Prices Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: I'd say Maghlaak is going to be a decent horse, jumping will toughen him up. His bit of class showed there late on and he did that well.  We bought him as a dual-purpose horse and he has a great pedigree - his dam won the Guineas - Adrian Keatley, trainer

quotes.race: Golf At Goodwood Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Maghlaak had a lot of weight, so did it well. I've no idea about plans - Jim Crowley, rider.

runners.spotlight: Made a winning start for this yard in a novice handicap chase at Southwell (2m4f, soft) last November; finished a long way behind Sea Of Kings at Doncaster on his return to the Flat four weeks ago; others appeal more.

stable_tour.quote: He finished well to win at Goodwood on his comeback, but he was drawn ten of ten at Redcar last time and could never get any cover. It was a non-event and I'm putting a line through it. He's a pretty talented horse, who likes to get his toe in, and I think the mile and a half would suit him well if he makes the cut. 13-06-24

He's been a good servant for us. He ran a good race in the Group 3 Silver Cup at York and then went so close at Market Rasen. I think if we keep stepping him up in trip, we'll get similar or better results with him. We'll look at the staying race at the Shergar Cup meeting and continue to mix it between hurdles and the Flat. He might jump fences in time. 07-08-25

runners.comment: 2m2f winner here last April; not so good since and others should have his measure today
runners.name: Diamand De Vindecy

prev_owners.owner: Nicolas Longere & Ecurie Haras Des Beaux

runners.spotlight: Ran away with a 2m2f handicap here last April; not quite so good since, including when well held back on the Flat at Ripon last month.

runners.comment: Can blow the start; not the force of old and others have more pressing claims
runners.name: Wahraan

prev_owners.owner: London Design Group Limited And Partner

runners.spotlight: Quirky and sometimes blows the start; on a reduced mark and retains some ability but he is not the obvious solution to this puzzle.

stable_tour.quote: He's very talented and an absolute rogue. He runs the most extraordinary races. At Southwell last week he was probably 30 lengths behind the last horse. He decided to lock on and ended up finishing third having run the most inefficient and energy-consuming race of all time. He'll drop right at some stage and I've just got to unlock his brain. If we can do that there's a good race in him off 84. 'd like to keep him on next year as we might just have a reset over the winter. I could see him charging through the handicap because he's got a lot of talent. 11-09-24

runners.breeder: The Rumble Racing Club - White Chocolate
runners.comment: AW hat-trick this winter and solid in defeat since; solid chance with headgear fitted
runners.name: Havachoc

quotes.race: Join The Midnite Movement Handicap (Rider Restricted Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: I got there quite nicely and he's won it easy, so I'm happy with that. Havachoc is a big, raw baby - Cian Horgan, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Completed a 1m4f AW hat-trick in January/February; series of good runs in defeat since, the latest when second at Wolverhampton two weeks ago; cheekpieces now given a go.

runners.comment: Good 3rd at Musselburgh on first Flat run for the yard; she now has something to build on
runners.name: Blondina
runners.spotlight: Modest maiden on the Flat in Ireland for Jim Bolger and showed little in three hurdles for current yard this year; last month's return to the Flat was much more encouraging though, keeping on strongly over 1m4f at Musselburgh, and she now has something to build on.

runners.comment: Won this race last year & continued on the up afterwards; not yet exposed; absent 309 days
runners.name: Dubai Venture
runners.spotlight: Made all to win the corresponding race 12 months ago off a 6lb lower mark; followed up at Beverley in July and only just denied in his hat-trick bid when last seen 309 days ago; races off the same mark here and there should be more to come this year.

runners.comment: Three wins from his last seven runs but he ran poorly over 2m last time; can bounce back
runners.name: Hickton
runners.spotlight: Took a while to get off the mark but he has won three of his last seven starts (1m4f-1m6f); poor run over 2m at Southwell two weeks ago; capable of bouncing back now dropping in distance.

runners.comment: 22-race maiden but he arrives on the back of two solid 3rd-place finishes; each-way shout
runners.name: Muhib
runners.spotlight: 0-22 but he arrives in good form, third in minor handicaps at Beverley and Catterick on his last two starts; more minor money could be forthcoming.

runners.comment: Not at best Flat or hurdles last month; drop in trip can help but others appeal more
runners.name: Lillistar
runners.spotlight: Not at her best over hurdles or here (extended 2m5f) last month; drop in trip can help but others appeal more for win purposes.

runners.comment: Exposed maiden; some good AW runs this year but behind Havachoc last time; opposable
runners.name: Apache Eagle

prev_owners.owner: Paul H Redmond & T G Fitzgerald & Mrs A M OBrien & B Fowler

runners.spotlight: 0-17 and he blows hot and cold but there have been some good runs in defeat on AW this year; finished behind Havachoc at Wolverhampton two weeks ago and may do so again.

runners.comment: 5 wins at up to 9.4f; stays 1m3f but likely there will be stronger stayers in the line up
runners.name: Anificas Beauty
runners.spotlight: Five wins at up to 9.4f; has form at 1m3f but suspicion there will be stronger stayers in the field.

runners.comment: Three C&D wins including this race last year; 1lb below last winning mark; contender
runners.name: Mount King

quotes.race: Every Raceday Is Autism Friendly At Pontefract Handicap
quotes.quote: Last time [met trouble at this course] was a disaster and the cheer I got on the way in I think every man and his dog spotted it and they've all had a few quid on! It went more smoothly today - a stronger gallop helped. Mount King  loves fast ground and he loves Pontefract - David Allan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Leslie Burton (Fisher) Handicap
quotes.quote: We bought Mount King second hand at the Horses In Training Sale from Joseph O'Brien and he's been a lovely horse for the owners - Tim Easterby, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Three of his four wins have come over C&D, including in this race 12 months ago; 1lb lower than for his last win and he should be at concert pitch with two runs under his belt; one for the shortlist.

runners.comment: C&D win last October worked out well; good return at Hamilton; yard hitting top form
runners.name: Arkenstaar

quotes.race: Hampton By Hilton Onsite Hotel Handicap
quotes.quote: We'll aim to go back to the track as Arkenstaar has never run a bad race there. I thought he showed a great attitude because he was being attacked from both sides. My biggest concern when speaking to Connor [Beasley, jockey] before was that there didn't look like there'd be any pace on, and he grinds it out more than anything. I'm really pleased with him, though - Michael Dods, trainer.

runners.spotlight: He was gaining his first win away from Hamilton when landing a C&D handicap last October off a 2lb lower mark; promising return to action at his beloved Hamilton 19 days ago; that should have blown away any cobwebs and he rates a strong contender for a yard who could be hitting top gear judged on recent results.

stable_tour.quote: He's won five races, all of them at Hamilton. There were no options at Hamilton recently but he likes a track with a hill finish - Hamilton, Carlisle, Pontefract, Beverley - so he ran last time out at Pontefract. He ran a good race in second behind Zozimus, a well-handicapped horse for David O'Meara. He just got shuffled out of it at the start and was probably further back than Connor Beasley would have liked but he came home strongly. I hope he can go one better next time. 28-08-24

runners.comment: Made all to win over C&D last month (visored first time); 2lb rise manageable
runners.name: Powerful Response

prev_owners.owner: J Kay T Goodair A Skelton C Johnson
Amo Racing Ltd Mrs Doyle Mr Morrin & PTN

runners.spotlight: Back to winning ways with a front-running C&D success 23 days ago (visored first time); up 2lb but should give it another good go.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 with two heavy defeats over 1m2f; down in trip/class for her return; chance
runners.name: Callisto Dream

quotes.race: Hoover Supporting Andersons Autumn Sale EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We haven't done a whole lot at home with Callisto Dream. We knew she was okay, but we haven't pressed a lot of buttons, so for her to come and do that first time out, there's plenty of improvement left - P J McDonald, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Won twice in novice company before running creditably in 1m handicaps at Ascot and Redcar last July; both subsequent runs have resulted in heavy defeats over 1m2f; returns from 222 days off at a lower level and back at a mile; not ruled out.

stable_tour.quote: She won by five lengths at Goodwood last time and the form has been franked. The fourth bolted up at Windsor last week and the second was third in the same race. I'm looking forward to running her again but have waited for the Coconut Fillies' Cup at Beverley this weekend. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Nottingham winner last October off 4lb lower; best run since when 4th in headgear latest
runners.name: Moonjid
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a breakthrough win at Nottingham (8.3f, good); ran his best race since when fourth back at Nottingham five weeks ago (cheekpieces first time); needs more to take this but it wouldn't be out of the question.

runners.comment: Course winner; not beaten far at Thirsk on Saturday; good draw; drying ground would help
runners.name: Selection

quotes.race: Northern Commercials Your Local Iveco Dealership EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice (GBB)(IRE Incentive)
quotes.quote: Selection was a very good buy, she only cost 8,000gns but she doesn't know that! She's a tough filly and she'll probably get further in time - Craig Lidster, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 6f course win as a 2yo; added a 1m handicap at Newcastle last October and there have been some near misses on AW this year too; not beaten far into fifth at Thirsk on Saturday on her return to Class 5 level; well drawn but slower than good would be a concern.

runners.comment: Four AW wins since December; return to 1m can help but no easy task off revised mark
runners.name: No Knee Never
runners.spotlight: Four wins (6f to 8.6f) on AW since December; perhaps stretched by 1m2f when only fourth at Ripon a fortnight ago; returning to a mile should help but a career best is needed to defy this mark.

runners.comment: Two Class 6 wins last season; sharper for last month's return but others still appeal more
runners.name: Keats House
runners.spotlight: Won two Class 6 handicaps at around 1m in the second half of 2025; creditable efforts off his revised mark to end that campaign and he should be sharper with last month's return to action behind him; others still appeal more for win purposes.

runners.comment: No threat on recent seasonal/h'cap debut but she was keeping on at the finish; unexposed
runners.name: Hopeful Joy
runners.spotlight: Looked rusty on her seasonal/handicap debut at Beverley ten days ago (8.4f, good to firm; 40-1); kept on well enough to think this mark was in range; not yet exposed.

runners.comment: Conditions fine and slipping back down the weights but yet to shine in 2026
runners.name: Distinction

prev_owners.owner: Nick Willis And Mike And Wendy Yardley

quotes.race: Charles Stewart & Co Steve Evans Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Distinction has done us proud. The stiff mile and soft ground were ideal. He's declared for Kempton tomorrow but that was just a back-up in case he couldn't run here - John Mackie, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Conditions no problem and he has slipped back down the weights but this year's efforts leave him with a point to prove.

16:57.race_name: CopyBet And Worcester Partners For 2026 Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners.comment: Unexposed 5yo and he needs a close look with tongue-tie added on chase debut
runners.name: Alba Crus
runners.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who was placed in a 2m3f novice hurdle last season; ran poorly on recent handicap hurdle debut (2m4f) and now has a point to prove but might be aided by first-time tongue-tie and connections are evidently keen to switch him to fences.

runners.comment: 0-9 but he's in the mix on best hurdles form; needs watching in market on chase debut
runners.name: Bongo Man
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden who has been inconsistent over hurdles but he was a close second in a Huntingdon handicap (2m, good; tongue-tie added) on his penultimate run; on same mark here and has possibilities if he can recapture that form on this switch to fences.

runners.comment: Hard to predict but was runner-up over fences (2m) on his penultimate run; in the mix
runners.name: Electric Eddy
runners.spotlight: Won a 2m handicap hurdle here (good) in September 2024; pulled up in two of his four starts since but he was runner-up over fences at Hereford (2m, good) on his penultimate run; that form puts him in the picture and this unexposed chaser is not ruled out after another break.

runners.comment: 17-race maiden under rules and was a well-held third at Hexham last time; others preferred
runners.name: Zero Tolerance
runners.spotlight: 17-race maiden under rules; reached the frame on numerous occasions over fences but he was beaten 21l when third at Hexham (1m7f, good to soft) two weeks ago; should be fine back on the forecast quicker ground but he needs to get back near his best.

runners.comment: Won at Taunton and he had an excuse when stepped back up to 2m4f latest; respected
runners.name: Applicationofcash

quotes.race: DragonBet Safer Gambling Tools No Roar Tonight Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: It's fantastic to get the first win. I've only had him less than two weeks. A jockeys' valet rang me and said Applicationofcash was for sale, I liked the look of his form and bought him from Connor Brace. I wasn't expecting him to win, I thought he would be better over two and a half miles, but it suited him today. I said to Rian that today is learning about him, but that will do his confidence the world of good. I prefer buying horses who are already handicapped and then tweaking a few things. We're a small team and we're just getting started. We'll have a few tonight to celebrate - Gordon Treacy, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 0-7 over hurdles but he made it fourth-time lucky over fences when scoring on his stable debut at Taunton (2m, good) in March; looked fortunate because the leader made a bad mistake at the last but he's only 2lb higher here and he had an excuse when stepped back up 2m4f last time; dangerous back in trip.

17:32.race_name: Safer Gambling At CopyBet Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Dual slow-ground chase winner at around 2m4f; good effort latest; each-way player.
runners.name: Atreides

quotes.race: Southern Cranes And Access Handicap Chase (Fontwell Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm very happy with Atreides and he showed a good attitude out there today. He jumped and travelled well and the visor seems to be having a good effect. We were always confident he'd handle conditions, as he has in the past. He's always given a good account of himself and he's done it nicely today - Neil Mulholland, trainer.
